1: Sing forth to Indu, O ye men, to him who now is purified, Fain to pay worship to the Gods!
Together with thy pleasant juice the Atharvans have commingled. milk. Divine, God-loving, for the God.
Bring health to cattle with thy flow, health to the people, health, to steeds, Health, O thou King, to growing plants!
Bright are these Somas blent with milk, with light that flashes brilliantly, And form that shouteth all around.
Roused by his drivers and sent forth, the strong Steed hath come: nigh for spoil, As warriors when they stand arrayed.
Specially, Soma, Sage, by day, coming together for our weal, Like Surya, flow for us to see!
The streams of Pavamana, thine, Sage, mighty one, have poured them forth, Like coursers eager for renown.
They have been poured upon the Reece towards the meath-distilling vat: The holy songs have rung aloud.
Like milch-kine coming home, the drops of Soma juice have reached the lake, Have reached the shrine of sacrifice
Come, Agni, praised with song to feast and sacrificial offerings: sit As Hotar on the holy grass!
So, Angiras, we make thee strong with fuel and with holy oil. Blaze high, thou youngest of the Gods!
For us thou winnest, Agni, God, heroic strength exceeding great, Far-spreading and of high renown.
Varuna, Mitra, sapient pair, pour fatness on our pastures, pour Meath on the regions of the air!
Gladdened by homage, ruling far, ye reign by majesty of might, Pure in your ways, for evermore.
Lauded by Jamadagni's song, sit in the shrine of sacrifice: Drink Soma, ye who strengthen Law!
Come, we have pressed theJuice for thee; O Indra, drink this Soma here: Sit thou on this my sacred grass!
O Indra, let thy long-maned bays, yoked by prayer, bring thee hitherward! Give ear and listen to our prayers!
We Soma-bearing Brahmans call thee Soma-drinker with thy friend, We, Indra, bringing Soma juice.
Indra and Agni, moved by songs, come to the juice, the precious dew: Drink ye thereof, impelled by prayer!
Indra and Agni, with the man who lauds comes visible sacrifice: So drink ye both this flowing juice!
With force of sacrifice I seek Indra, Agni who love the wise: With Soma let them sate them here!
High is thy juice's birth: though set in heaven, on earth it hath obtained Dread sheltering power and great renown.
Finder of room and freedom, flow for Indra whom we must adore, For Varuna and the Marut host!
Striving to win, with him we gain all riches from the enemy, Yea, all the glories of mankind,
Cleansing thee, Soma, in thy stream, thou flowest in watery robe. Giver of wealth, thou sittest in the place of Law, O God, a fountain made of gold.
He, milking for dear meath the heavenly udder, hath sat in the ancient gathering-place. Washed by the men, far-sighted, strong, thou streamest to ther honourable reservoir.
Run onward to the reservoir and seat thee: cleansed by the men speed forward to the battle. Making thee glossy like an able courser, forth to the sacred grass with reins they lead thee.
Indu, the well-armed God is flowing onward, he who averts the curse and guards the homesteads. Father, begetter of the Gods, most skilful, the buttress of the heavens and earth's supporter.
Like kine unmilked we call aloud, hero, to thee, and sing thy praise, Looker on heavenly light, Lord of this moving world, Lord, Indra! of what moveth not.
None other like to thee, of earth or of the heavens, hath been or ever will be born. Desiring horses, Indra Maghavan! and kine, as men of might we call on thee.
With what help will he come to us, wonderful, everwaxing friend? With what most mighty company?
What genuine and most liberal draught will spirit thee with juice to burst Open e'en strongly-guarded wealth?
Do thou who art protector of us thy friends who praise thee With hundred aids approach us!
As cows low to their calves in stalls, so with our songs we glorify This Indra, even your wondrous God who checks attack, who takes delight in precious juice.
Celestial, bounteous giver, girt about with might, rich, mountain-like, in pleasant things,-- Him swift we seek for foodful booty rich in kine, brought hundredfold and thousandfold.
Loud-singing at tbe sacred rite where Soma flows, we priests invoke. With haste, that he may help, as the bard's cherisher. Indra who findeth wealth for you.
Whom, fair of cheek, in rapture of the juice, the firm resistless slayers hinder not: Giver of glorious wealth to him who sings his praise, honouring him who toils and pours.
In sweetest and most gladdening stream flow pure, O Soma, on thy way, Pressed out for Indra, for his drink!
Fiend-queller, friend of all men, he hath reached his shrine, his dwelling-place. Within the iron-hammered vat.
Be thou best Vritra-slaver, best granter of room, most liberal: Promote our wealthy princes' gifts!
For Indra flow, thou Soma, on, as most inspiring drink, most rich in sweets, Great, most Celestial, gladdening drink!
Thou of whom having drunk the Steer acts like a steer: having drunk this that finds the light, He, excellently wise, hath come anear to food and booty, even as Etasa.
To Indra, to the mighty let these golden-coloured juices go, Drops born as Law prescribes, that find the light of heaven!
This juice that gathers spoil flows, pressed, for Indra, for his maintenance. Soma bethinks him of the conqueror, as he knows.
Yea, Indra in the joys of this obtains the grasp that gathers spoil, And, winning waters, wields the mighty thunderbolt.
For first possession of your juice, for the exhilarating drink, Drive ye away the dog, my friends, drive ye the long-tongued dog away!
He who with purifying stream, effused, comes flowing hitherward, Indu, is like an able steed.
With prayer all-reaching let the men tend unassailable Soma: be- The stones prepared for sacrifice!
Graciously- minded he is flowing on his way to win dear names o'er which the youthful one grows great. The mighty and far-seeing one hath mounted now the mighty Surya's car which moves to every side.

The speaker, unassailable master of this prayer, the tongue of sacrifice, pours forth the pleasant meath. As son be sets the name of mother and of sire in the far distance, in the third bright realm of heaven.

Sending forth flashes he hath bellowed to the jars, led by the men into the golden reservoir. The milkers of the sacrifice have sung to him: Lord of three heights, thou shinest brightly o'er the Dawns.
Sing to your Agni with each song, at every sacrifice for strength! Come, let us praise the wise and everlasting God, even as a well-beloved friend:
The Son of Strength; for is be not our gracious Lord? Let us serve him who bears our gifts! In battles may he be our help and strengthener, yea, be the saviour of our lives!
O Agni, come; far other songs of praise will I sing forth to thee. Wax mighty with these Soma drops!
Where'er thy mind applies itself, vigour preeminent hast thou: There wilt thou gain a dwelling-place.
Not for a moment only lasts thy bounty, Lord of many men: Our service therefore shalt thou gain.
We call on thee, O matchless one. We, seeking help, possessing nothing firm ourselves. Call on thee, wondrous, thunder-armed:
On thee for aid in sacrifice, This youth of ours, the bold, the terrible, bath gone forth. We therefore, we thy friends, Indra, have chosen thee, spoil winner, as our succourer.
So, Indra, friend of song, do we draw near to thee with longing; we have streamed to thee Coming like floods that follow floods.
As rivers swell the ocean, so, hero, our prayers increase thy might, Though of thyself, O Thunderer, waxing day by day.
With holy song they bind to the broad wide-yoked car the bay steeds of the quickening God, Bearers of Indra, yoked by word.
Invite ye Indra with a song to drink your draught of Soma juice, All-conquering Satakratu, most munificent of all who live!
Lauded by many, much-invoked, leader of song renowned of old: His name is Indra, tell it forth!
Indra, the dancer, be to us the giver of abundant wealth: The mighty bring it us knee-deep!
Sing ye a song, to make him glad, to Indra, Lord of tawny steeds, The Soma-drinker, O my friends!
To him, the bounteous, say the laud, and let us glorify, as men May do, the giver of true gifts!
O Indra, Lord of boundless might, for us thou seekest spoil and kine, Thou seekest gold for us, good Lord!
This, even this, O Indra, we implore: as thy devoted friends, The Kanvas praise thee with their hymns.
Naught else, O Thunderer, have I praised in the skilled singer's eulogy; On thy laud only have I thought.
The Gods seek him who presses out the Soma; they desire not sleep: They punish sloth unweariedly
For Indra, lover of carouse, loud be our songs about the juice: Let poets sing the song of praise
We summon Indra to the draught, in whom all glories rest, in whom The seven communities rejoice.
At the Trikadrukas the Gods span sacrifice that stirs the mind: Let our songs aid and prosper it!
Here, Indra, is thy Soma draught, made pure upon the sacred grass: Run hither, come and drink thereof!
Strong-rayed! adored with earnest hymns! this juice is shed for thy delight: Thou art invoked, Akhandala!
To Kundapayya, grandson's son, grandson of Sringavrish! to thee, To him have I addressed my thought.
Indra, as one with mighty arm, gather for us with thy right hand, Manifold and nutritious spoil!
We know thee mighty in thy deeds, of mighty bounty, mighty wealth. Mighty in measure, prompt to aid.
Hero when thou wouldst give thy gifts, neither the Gods nor mortal men Restrain thee like a fearful bull.
Hero, the Soma being shed, I pour the juice for thee to drink: Sate thee and finish thy carouse!
Let not the fools, or those who mock, beguile thee when they seek thine aid: Love not the enemy of prayer!
Here let them cheer thee well supplied with milk to great munificence: Drink as the wild bull drinks the lake!
Here is the Soma juice expressed: O Vasu, drink till thou art full! Undaunted God, we give it thee!
Washed by the men, pressed out with stones, strained through the filter made of wool, 'Tis like a courser bathed in streams.
This juice have we made sweet for thee like barley, blending it with milk. Indra, I call thee to our feast.
So, Lord of affluent gifts, this juice hath been expressed for thee with strength: Drink of it, thou who lovest song!
Incline thy body to the juice which suits thy godlike nature well: Thee, Soma-lover! let it cheer!
O Indra, let it enter both thy flanks, enter thy head with prayer, With bounty, hero! both thine arms!
O Come ye hither, sit ye down; to Indra sing ye forth your song, Companions, bringing hymns of praise,
Laud Indra, richest of the rich, who ruleth over noblest wealth, Beside the flowing Soma juice!
May he stand near us in our need with all abundance, for our wealth: With strength may he come nigh to us!
In every need, in every fray we call, as friends to succour us, Indra, the mightiest of all.
I call him, mighty to resist, the hero of our ancient home, Thee whom my sire invoked of old.
If he will hear us, let him come with succour of a thousand kinds, With strength and riches, to our call!
When Somas flow thou makest pure, Indra, thy mind that merits laud, For gain of strength that ever grows: for great is he.
In heaven's first region, in the seat of Gods, is he who brings success, Most glorious, prompt to save, who wins the waterfloods.
Him I invoke, to win the spoil, even mighty Indra for the fray. Be thou most near to us for bliss, a friend to aid!
With this mine homage I invoke Agni for you, the Son of Strength. Dear, wisest envoy, skilled in noble sacrifice, immortal, messenger of all.
His two red horses, all-supporting, let him yoke: let him, well-worshipped, urge them fast! Then hath the sacrifice good prayers and happy end, the heavenly gift of wealth to men.
Advancing, sending forth her rays, the daughter of the Sky is seen. The mighty one lays bare the darkness with her eye, the friendly Lady makes the light.
The Sun ascending, the refulgent star, pours down his beams. together with the Dawn. O Dawn, at thine arising, and, the Sun's, may we attain the share allotted us!
These morning sacrifices call you, Asvins, at the break of day. For help have I invoked you rich in power and might: for, house by house, ye visit all.
Ye, heroes, have bestowed wonderful nourishment: send it to him whose songs are sweet. One-minded, both of you, drive your car down to us: drink yethe savoury Soma juice!
After his ancient splendour, they, the bold, have drawn the bright milk from The Sage who wins a thousand spoils.
In aspect he is like the Sun: he runneth forward to the lakes: Seven currents flowing to the sky.
He, while they purify him, stands high over all things that exist Soma, a God as Surya is.
By generation long ago this God, engendered for the Gods, Flows tawny to the straining cloth.
According to primeval plan this poet hath been strengthened by, The sage as God for all the Gods.
Shedding the ancient fiuid thou art poured into the cleansing sieve: Roaring, thou hast produced the Gods.
Bring near us those who stand aloof: strike fear into our enemy: O Pavamana, find us wealth!
To him the active, nobly born.
Sing ye your songs to him, O men!
The Somas skilled in song, the waves have led the water forward, like Buffaloes speeding to the woods.
With stream of sacrifice the brown bright drops have flowed with strength in store Of kine into the wooden vats.
To Indra, Vayu. Varuna to Vishnu and the Maruts let The Soma juices flow expressed.
O Soma, for the feast of Gods, river-like he hath swelled with surge, Sweet with the liquor of the stalk, as one who wakes, into the vat that drops with meath.
Like a dear son how must be decked, the bright and shining one hath clad him in his robe. Men skilful at their work drive him forth, like a car, into the rivers from their hands.
The rapture-shedding Somas have flowed forth in our assembly, pressed. To glorify our liberal lords.
Now like a swan hemaketh all the company sing each his hymm He like steed is bathed in milk.
And Trita's maidens onward urge the tawny-coloured with the stones, Indu for Indra, for his drink.
Herewith flow on, thou friend of Gods! Singing, thou runnest round the sieve oni every side. The streams of meath have been effused.
For him who presses, of the juice.

Chapter I · Hymn 1.1

Do thou as leader of the song, stirring the waters of the sea, Flow onward, known to all mankind! 1 O Soma, O thou Sage, these worlds stand ready to enhance thy might: The milch-kine run for thy behoof.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.2
Indu, flow on, a mighty juice; glorify us among the folk: Drive all our enernies away!
Chapter I · Hymn 2.1
And in thy friendship, Indu, most sublime and glorious, may we Subdue all those who war with us!
Chapter I · Hymn 2.2
Those awful weapons which thou hast, sharpened at point to strike men down-- Guard us therewith from every foe!
Chapter I · Hymn 2.3
O Soma, thou art strong and bright, potent, O God, with potent sway,
Chapter I · Hymn 3.1
Steer-strong thy might is like a steer's, steer-strong the wood, steer-strong the juice: A steer indeed, O Steer, art thou.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.2
Thou, Indu, as a vigorous horse, hast neighed together steeds and kine: Unbar for us the doors to wealth!
Chapter I · Hymn 3.3
For thou art strong by splendour: we, O Pavamana call on thee, The brilliant looker on the light.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.1
When thou art sprinkled with the streams, thou reachest, purified by men, Thy dwelling in the wooden vat.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.2
Do thou, rejoicing, nobly-armed! pour upon us heroic strength. O Indu, come thou hitherward!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.3
We seek to win thy friendly love, even Pavamana's flowing o'er The limit of the cleansing sieve.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.1
With those same waves which in their stream o'erflow the purifying sieve, Soma, be gracious unto us!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.2
O Soma, being purified, bring us from all sides-for thou canst- Riches and food with hero sons!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.3
Agni we choose as envoy, skilled performer of this holy rite, Hotar, possessor of all wealth.
Chapter I · Hymn 6.1
With constant calls they invocate Agni, Agni, Lord of the house, Oblation-bearer, much-beloved
Chapter I · Hymn 6.2
Bring the Gods hither, Agni, born for him who trims the Sacred grass: Thou art our Hotar, meet for praise!
Chapter I · Hymn 6.3
Mitra and Varuna we call to drink the draught of Soma juice, Those born endowed with holy strength.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.1
Those who by Law uphold the Law, Lords of the shining light of Law, Mitra I call, and Varuna.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.2
Let Varuna be our chief defence, let Mitra guard us with all aids, Both make us rich exceedingly!
Chapter I · Hymn 7.3
Indra the singers with high praise, Indra reciters with their lauds, Indra the choirs have glorified.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.1
Indra is close to his two bays, with chariot ready at his word, Indra the golden, thunder-armed.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.2
Help us in battles Indra, in battles where thousand spoils are gained, With awful aids, O awful one!
Chapter I · Hymn 8.3
Indra raised up the son aloft in heaven, that he may see afar: He burst the mountain for the kine.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.4
To Indra and to Agni we bring reverence high and holy hymn, And, craving help, soft words with prayer.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.1
For all these holy singers thus implore these twain to succour them, And priests that they may win them strength.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.2
Eager to laud you, we with songs invoke you, bearing sacred food, Fain for success in sacrifice.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.3
Flow onward, mighty with thy stream, inspiriting the Marut's Lord, Winning all riches with thy power!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.1
I send thee forth to battle from the press, O Pavamana, strong, Sustainer, looker on the light!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.2
Acknowledged by this song of mine, flow, tawnycoloured, with thy stream: Incite to battle thine ally!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.3
A Red Bull bellowing to the kine, thou goest, causing the heavens and earth to roar and thunder. A shout is heard like Indra's in the battle: thou flowest on, sending this voice before thee.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.1
Swelling with milk, abounding in sweet juices, urging the meathrich plant thou goest onward. Making loud clamour, Soma Pavamana, thou flowest when thou art effused for Indra.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.2
So flow thou on inspiriting, for rapture, turning the weapon of the water's holder! Flow to us wearing thy resplendent colour, effused and eager for the kine. O Soma!
Chapter I · Hymn 11.3
That we may win us wealth and power we poets verily, call on thee: In war men call on thee, Indra, the hero's Lord, in the steed's race-course call on thee
Chapter I · Hymn 12.1
As such, O wonderful, whose hand holds thunder, praised as mighty, Caster of the Stone! Pour on us boldly, Indra, kine and chariot-steeds, ever to be the conqueror's strength!
Chapter I · Hymn 12.2
To you will I sing Indra's praise who gives good gifts, as we I we know; The praise of Maghavan who, rich in treasure, aids his singers with wealth thousandfold.
Chapter I · Hymn 13.1
As with a hundred hosts, he rushes boldly on, and for the offerer slays his foes. As from a mountain fiow the water-brooks, thus flow his gifts who feedeth many a one.
Chapter I · Hymn 13.2
O Thunderer, zealous worshippers gave thee drink this time yesterday: So, Indra, listen here to him who offers lauds: come near unto our dwelling-place!
Chapter I · Hymn 14.1
Lord of bay steeds, fair-helmed, rejoice thee: thee we seek. Here the disposers wait on thee. Thy glories, meet for praise! are highest by the juice, O Indra, lover of the song.
Chapter I · Hymn 14.2
Flow onward with that juice of thine most excellent, that brings delight, Slaying the wicked, dear to Gods!
Chapter I · Hymn 15.1
Killing the foeman and his hate, and daily winning spoil and strength, Gainer art thou of steeds and kine.
Chapter I · Hymn 15.2
Red-hued, be blended with the milk that seems to yield its lovely breast, Falcon-like resting in thine home!
Chapter I · Hymn 15.3
As Pashan, Fortune, Bhaga, comes this Soma while they make him pure. He, Lord of all the multitude, hath looked upon the earth and heaven.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.1
The dear cows sang in joyful mood together to the gladdening drink. The drops as they are purified, the Soma juices, make the paths.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.2
O Pavamana, bring the juice, the mightiest, worthy to be famed, Which the Five Tribes have over them, whereby we may win opulence!
Chapter I · Hymn 16.3

Far-seeing Soma flows, the Steer, the Lord of hymns, the furtherer of days, of mornings, and of heaven. Breath of the rivers, he hath roared into the jars, and with the help of sages entered Indra's heart.
Chapter I · Hymn 17.1

On, with the sages, flows the poet on his way, and guided by the men, hath streamed into the vats. He, showing Trita's name, hath caused the meath to flow, increasing Vayu's strength to make him Indra's friend.
Chapter I · Hymn 17.2

He, being purified, hath made the mornings shine, and it is he who gave the rivers room to flow. Making the three-times seven pour out the milky stream, Soma, the cheerer, yields whate'er the heart finds sweet.
Chapter I · Hymn 17.3
For so thou art the brave man's friend; a hero, too, art thou, and strong: So may thy heart be won us!
Chapter I · Hymn 18.1
So hath the offering. wealthiest Lord, been paid by all the worshippers. So dwell thou, Indra, even with us!
Chapter I · Hymn 18.2
Be not thou like a slothful priest, O Lord of spoil and strength: rejoice In the pressed Soma blent with milk!
Chapter I · Hymn 18.3
All sacred songs have magnified Indra expansive as the sea. Best of all warriors borne on cars, the Lord of heroes, Lord of strength.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.1
Lord of might, Indra, may we ne'er, strong in thy friendship, be afraid! We glorify with praises thee, the never conquered conqueror.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.2
The gifts of Indra from of old, his saving succours never fail, When to his worshippers he gives the boon of booty rich in kine.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.3
These rapid Soma-drops have been poured through the purifying sieve. To bring us all felicities.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.1
Dispelling manifold mishap, giving the courser's progeny, Yea, and the warrior steed's, success.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.2
Bringing prosperity to kine, they pour perpetual strengthening food On us for noble eulogy.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.3
King Pavamana is implored with holy songs, on man's behalf, To travel through, the realm of air.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.1
Pressed for the banquet of the Gods, O Soma, bring us might,and speed, Like beauty for a'brilliant show!
Chapter II · Hymn 2.2
Bring us, O Indu, hundredfold increase of kine, and noble steeds. The gift of fortune for our help!
Chapter II · Hymn 2.3
With sacrifice we seek to thee fair cherisher of manly might In mansons of the lofty heavens.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.1
Drink gladdening, crusher of the bold, praiseworthy, with most mighty sway, Destroyer of a hundred forts.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.2
Hence riches came to thee, the King, O sapient one: the strong-winged bird, Unwearied, brought thee from the sky.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.3
And now, sent forth, he hath attained to mighty power and majesty, Active and ready to assist.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.4
That each may see the light, the bird brought us the guard of Law, the friend O fall, the speeder through the air.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.5
For food, flow onward with thy stream, cleansed and made bright by sapient men: Indu, with sheen approach the milk!
Chapter II · Hymn 4.1
While thou art cleansed, song-lover. bring comfort and vigourto the folk, Poured, tawny one! on milk and curds!
Chapter II · Hymn 4.2
Purified for feast of Gods, go thou to Indra's resting-place, Resplendent, furthered by the strong!
Chapter II · Hymn 4.3
By Agni Agni is inflamed, Lord of the house, wise, young,. who bears Our gifts: the ladle is his mouth.
Chapter II · Hymn 5.1
God, Agni, be his sure defence who, lord of sacrificial gifts. Worshippeth thee the messenger.
Chapter II · Hymn 5.2
Be gracious, brilliant Godl to him who, rich in sacred gifts,would fain Call Agni to the feast of Gods!
Chapter II · Hymn 5.3
Mitra of holy strength I call, and foe-destroying Varuna, Who perfect prayer with offered oil.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.1
By Law, O Mitra, Varuna, Law-strengtheners who cleave to Law, Have ye obtained your lofty power.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.2
The Sages, Mitra, Varuna, of wide dominion, mighty ones, Bestow on us effectual strength.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.3
So mayst thou verily be seen coming with fearless Indra: both Of equal splendour, bringing bliss!
Chapter II · Hymn 7.1
Thereafter they, as is their wont, resumed the state of new-born babes, Taking their sacrificial name.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.2
Thou, Indra, with the rapid Gods who shatter even what is firm, Even in the cave didst find the cows.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.3
I call the twain whose deed wrought here hath all been famed in ancient time: Indra and Agni harm us not!
Chapter II · Hymn 8.1
The strong, the scatterers of the foe, Indra and Agni we invoke: May they be kind to one like me:
Chapter II · Hymn 8.2
Ye slay our Arya foes, O Lords of heroes, slay our Dasa foes: Ye drive all enemies away.
Chapter II · Hymn 8.3
The living drops of Soma juice pour, as they flow the gladdening drink, Intelligent drops above the station of the sea, exhilarating, dropping meath.
Chapter II · Hymn 9.1
May Pavamana, King and God, speed with his wave over the sea the lofty rite! Do thou by Mitra's and by Varuna's decree flow furthering the lofty rite:
Chapter II · Hymn 9.2
Far-seeing, lovely, guided by the men, the God whose habitation is the sea!
Chapter II · Hymn 9.3
Three are the voices that the car-steed utters: he speaks the lore of prayer, the thought of Order. To the cows' master come the cows inquiring: the hymns with eager longing come to Soma.
Chapter II · Hymn 10.1
To Soma come the cows, the milch-kine longing, to Soma sages with their hymns inquiring. Soma, effused, is purified and lauded: our hymns and Trishtup songs unite in Soma.
Chapter II · Hymn 10.2
Thus, Soma, as we pour thee into vessels, while thou art purified, flow for our welfare! Pass into Indra. with great joy and rapture: make the voice swell, and generate abundance!
Chapter II · Hymn 10.3
O Indra, if a hundred heavens and if a hundred earths were thine,-- No, not a hundred suns could match thee at thy birth, not both the worlds, O Thunderer.
Chapter II · Hymn 11.1
Thou, hero, hast performed thy hero deeds with might, yea, all with strength, O strongest one. Maghavan, help us to a stable full of kine, O Thunderer, with wondrous aids!
Chapter II · Hymn 11.2
We compass thee like water, we whose grass is trimmed and Soma pressed. Here where the filter pours its stream, thy worshippers round thee, O Vritra-slayer, sit.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.1
Men, Vasu! by the Soma with lauds call thee to the foremost place. When cometh he athirst unto the juice as home, O Indra, like a bellowing bull?
Chapter II · Hymn 12.2
O valiant hero, boldly win thousandfold spoil with Kanva's sons! O active Maghavan, with eager prayer we crave the yellowhued with store of kine.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.3
With Plenty for his true ally the active man will gain the spoil. Your Indra, much-invoked, I bend with song, as bends a wright his wheel of solid wood.
Chapter II · Hymn 13.1
They who bestow great riches love not paltry praise: wealth comes not to the niggard churl. Light is the task to give, O Maghavan, to one like me on the decisive day.
Chapter II · Hymn 13.2
Three several words are uttered: kine are lowing cows. who give the milk: The tawny-hued goes bellowing on.
Chapter II · Hymn 14.1
The young and sacred mothers of the holy rite have uttered praise, Embellishing the Child of Heaven.
Chapter II · Hymn 14.2
From every side, O Soma, for our profit, pour thou forth four seas. Filled full of riches thousandfold!
Chapter II · Hymn 14.3
The Somas, very rich in sweets, for which the sieve is distined, flow Effused, the source of Indra's joy: may you strong juices reach the Gods!
Chapter II · Hymn 15.1
Indu flows on for Indra's sake,-thus have the deities declared. The Lord of Speech exerts himself, controller of all power and might.
Chapter II · Hymn 15.2
Inciter of the voice of song, with thousand streams the ocean flows. Even Soma, Lord of opulence, the friend of Indra, day by day.
Chapter II · Hymn 15.3

SPREAD is thy cleansing filter, Brahmanaspati: as prince thou enterest its limbs from every side. The raw; whose mass bath not been heated. gains not this: they only which are dressed, which bear, attain to it.
Chapter II · Hymn 16.1

High in the seat of heaven is placed the scorcher's sieve: its, threads are standing separate, glittering with light. The swift ones favour him who purifieth this: with brilliancy they mount up to the height of heaven.
Chapter II · Hymn 16.2

The foremost spotted Steer bath made the Mornings shine: he bellows, fain for war, among created things. By his high wisdom have the mighty Sages wrought: the Fathers who behold mankind laid down the germ.
Chapter II · Hymn 16.3
Sing forth to him, the holy, most munificent, sublime with his refulgent glow, To Agni, ye Upastutas
Chapter II · Hymn 17.1
Worshipped with gifts, enkindled, splendid, Maghavan shall win himself heroic fame: And will not his more plentiful benevolence come to us with abundant strength?
Chapter II · Hymn 17.2
We sing this strong and wild delight of thine which conquers in the fray, Which, Caster of the Stone! gives room and shines like gold.
Chapter II · Hymn 18.1
Wherewith thou foundest shining lights for Ayu and for Manu's sake: Now joying in this sacred grass thou bearnest forth.
Chapter II · Hymn 18.2
This day too singers of the hymn praise, as of old, this might of thine: Win thou the waters every day, thralls of the strong!
Chapter II · Hymn 18.3
O Indra, hear Tirschi's call, the call of him who serveth thee. Satisfy him with wealth of kine and valient offspring! Great art thou.
Chapter II · Hymn 19.1
For he, O Indra, hath produced for thee the newest gladdening song, A hymn that springs from careful drop thought, ancient and full of sacred truth.
Chapter II · Hymn 19.2
That Indra will we laud whom songs and hymns of praise have magnified. Striving to win, we celebrate his many deeds of hero might.
Chapter II · Hymn 19.3
3: Fleet as swift steeds thy cows celestial have been poured, O Pavamana, with the milk into the vat. Sages who make thee bright, O friend whom Rishis love, have shed continuous streams from out the realm of air.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.1

The beams of Pavamana, sent from earth and heaven his ensigns who is ever stedfast, travel round. When on the sieve the golden-hued is cleansed he rests within the jars as one who seats him in his place.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.2

O thou who seest all things, sovran as thou art and passing strong, thy rays encompass every form. Pervading with thy natural powers thou flowest on, and as the whole world's Lord, O Soma, thou art King.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.3
From heaven hath Pavamana, made, as 'twere, the marvellous thunder, and The lofty light of all mankind.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.1
The gladdening and auspicious juice of thee, O Pavamana, King! Flows o'cr the woollen straining-cloth.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.2
Thy juice, O Pavamana, sends its rays abroad fixe splendid skill, Like lustre, all heaven's light, to see.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.3
Impetuous, bright, have they come forth, unwearied in their speed, like bulls, Driving the black skin far away.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.1
May we attain the bridge of bliss, leaving the bridge of woe behind: The riteless Dasa may we quell!
Chapter I · Hymn 3.2
The mighty Pavamana's roar is heard as 'twere the rush of rain The lightning-Rashes move in heaven.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.3
Indu, pour out abundant food with store of cattle and of gold, Of heroes, Soma! and of steeds!
Chapter I · Hymn 3.4
Flow onward, dear to all mankind fi full the mighty heaven and earth, As Dawn, as Surya with his beams
Chapter I · Hymn 3.5
On every side, O Soma, flow round us with thy protecting stream, As Rasa flows around the world!
Chapter I · Hymn 3.6
Flow on, O thou of lofty thought, flow swift in thy beloved form, Saying, I go where dwell the Gods.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.1
Preparing what is unprepared, and bringing store of food to man, Make thou the rain descend from heaven
Chapter I · Hymn 4.2
Even here is he who, swift of course, hath with the river's wave Rowed down. From heaven upon the straining cloth.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.3
With might. producing glare, the juice enters the purifying sieve, Far-seeing, sending forth its light.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.4
Inviting him from far away, and even from near at hand, the juice For Indra is poured forth as meath.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.5
In union they have sung the hymn: with stones they urge the golden-hued, Indu for Indra, for his drink.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.6
The glittering maids send Sdra forth, the glorious sisters, closeallied, Send Indu forth, their mighty Lord.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.1
Pervade, O Pavamana, all our treasures with repeated light, Pressed out, O God thyself, for Gods!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.2
Pour on us, Pavamana! rain, as service and fair praise for Gods: Pour forth unceasingly for food!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.3

The watchful guardian of the people hath been born, Agni, the very strong, for fresh prosperity. With oil upon his face. with high heaven-touching flame, he shineth splendidly, pure, for the Bharatas.
Chapter I · Hymn 6.1

O Agni, the Angirasas discovered thee what time thou layest hidden, fleeing back from wood to wood. Thou by attrition art produced as conquering might, and men, O Angiras, call thee the Son of Strength.
Chapter I · Hymn 6.2
The men enkindle Agni in his threefold seat, ensign of sacrifice, the earliest bousehold- priest. With Indra and the Gods together on the grass let the wise priest sit to complete the sacrifice!
Chapter I · Hymn 6.3
This Soma hath been pressed for you, Low-strengtheners, Mitra, Varuna! List, list ye here to this may call!
Chapter I · Hymn 7.1
Both Kings who never injure aught have come to their sublimest home, The thousand-pillared, firmly based.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.2
Worshipped with fat libation. Lords of gifts, Adityas, sovran Kings, They wait on him whose life is true.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.3
Armed with the bones of dead Dadhyach, Indra with unresisted. might The nine-and-ninety Vritras slew.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.1
He, searching for the horse's head that in the mountains lay concealed, Found it in Saryandvdn lake.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.2
Then straight they recognized the mystic name of the creative Steer. There in the mansion of the Moon.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.3
As rain from out the cloud, for you, Indra and Agni, from my thought This noblest praise hath been produced.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.1
Indra and Agni, listen to the singer's call: accept his songs. Fulfil, ye mighty Lords, his prayers!
Chapter I · Hymn 9.2
Give us not up to indigence, ye heroes, Indra, Agni, nor To Slander and reproach of men!
Chapter I · Hymn 9.3
Gold-Hued! as one who giveth strength flow on for Gods to drink, a draught For Vayu and the Marut host!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.1
The Steer shines brightly with the Gods, dear Sage in his appointed home. Even Pavamana unbeguiled.
Chapter I · Hymn 10.2
O Pavamana, sent by prayer, roaring about thy dwelling-place, Ascend to Vayu as Law bids!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.3
O Soma, Indu, every day thy friendship hath been my delight. Many fiends follow me; help me, thou tawny-hued: pass on beyond these barriers!
Chapter I · Hymn 11.1
Close to thy bosom am I. Soma, day and night draining the milk, O golden hued. Surya himself refulgent with his glow have we, as birds, o'ertaken in his course.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.2
Active, while being purified, he hath assailed all enemies: They deck the Sage with holy hymns.
Chapter I · Hymn 12.1
The Red hath mounted to his shrine; strong Indra hath approached the juice: In his firm dwelling let him rest!
Chapter I · Hymn 12.2
O Indu, Soma, send us now great opulence from every side: Pour on us treasures thousandfold!
Chapter I · Hymn 12.3
Drink Soma, Indra Lord of bays! and let it cheer thee: the stone, like a well-guided courser, Directed by the presser's arms bath pressed it.
Chapter I · Hymn 13.1
So let the draught of joy, thy dear companion, by which, O Lord of bays, thou slayest Vritras, Delight thee, Indra, Lord of princely treasuresl
Chapter I · Hymn 13.2
Mark closely, Maghavan, the word I utter, this eulogy recited by Vasislitha: Accept the prayers I offer at thy banquet!
Chapter I · Hymn 13.3

Heroes of one accord brought forth and formed for kingship Indra who wins the victory in all encounters, For power, in firmness, in the field, the great destroyer, fierce and exceeding strong, stalwart and full of vigour.
Chapter I · Hymn 14.1
The holy sages form a ring, to view and sing unto the Ram. Inciters, very brilliant, from all deceit, are with your chariters nigh to hear.
Chapter I · Hymn 14.2
Bards joined in song to Indra so that he might drink the Soma juice. The Lord of light, that he whose laws stand fast might aid with power and with the help he gives.
Chapter I · Hymn 14.3
He who as sovran Lord of men moves with his chariots unrestrained, The Vritra-slayer, vanquisher of all fighting hosts, pre-eminent, is praised in song.
Chapter I · Hymn 15.1
Honour that Indra, Puruhanman! for his aid, him in whose hand of old the fair Sustaining bolt of thunder, mighty like the God, like Surya, was deposited!
Chapter I · Hymn 15.2
The Sage of heaven whose heart is wise, when laid between both hands, with roars, Gives us delightful powers of life.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.1
He, the bright son, when born, illumed his parents who had sprung to life, Great Son, great strengtheners of Law.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.2
On, onward to a glorious home, free from all guile and dear to. men, Flow with enjoyment to our praise!
Chapter I · Hymn 16.3
For, verily, Pavamana, thou, divine! endued with brightest splendour, calling all Creatures to immortality.
Chapter I · Hymn 17.1
With whom Dadhyach Navagva opened fastened doors, by whom the sages gained their wish, By whom they won the fame of lovely Amrita in the felicity of Gods.
Chapter I · Hymn 17.4
Soma, while filtered, with his wave flows through the long wool of the sheep, Roaring, while purified, before the voice of song.
Chapter I · Hymn 18.1
With prayers they cleanse the mighty steed, sporting in wood, above the fleece: Our hymns, intoned, have praised him of the triple height.
Chapter I · Hymn 18.2
He hath been hastened to the jars, bountiful, like an eager horse, And, lifting up his voice, while filtered, glided on.
Chapter I · Hymn 18.3
Father of holy hymns, Soma flows onward, the father of the earth, father of heaven. Father of Agni, Surya's generator, the father who begat Indra and Vishnu.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.1
Brahman of Gods, the leader of the poets, Rishi of sages, chief of savage creatures, Falcon amid the vultures, axe of forests, over the cleansing sieve goes Soma singing.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.2
He, Soma Pavamana, like a river, hath stirred the wave of voice, our songs and praises Beholding these inferior powers, the hero, well knowing, takes his stand among the cattle.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.3
Hither, for powerful kinship, I call Agni, him who prospers you, Most frequent at our solemn rites.
Chapter I · Hymn 20.1
That through this famed one's power he may stand by us, even as Tvasbtar comes Unto the forms that must be shaped.
Chapter I · Hymn 20.2
This Agni is the Lord supreme above all glories' mid the Gods: May he come nigh to us with strength.
Chapter I · Hymn 20.3
This poured libation, Indra drink, immortal, gladdening, excellent! Streams of the bright have flowed to thee here at the seat of holy Law.
Chapter I · Hymn 21.1
When, Indra, thou dost guide thy bays, there is no better charioteer: None hath surpassed thee in thy might, none with good steeds o'ertaken thee.
Chapter I · Hymn 21.2
Sing glory now to Indra, say to him your solemn eulogies! The drops poured forth have made him glad: pay reverence to his noblest might!
Chapter I · Hymn 21.3
Indra, be pleased: drive forward, hero, striker of thy bays! Fair, like a sage, delighting in the meath, drink of the juice for rapturous joy.
Chapter I · Hymn 22.1
O Indra, fill thy belly anew with meath that seems to flow from heaven. The sweet-voiced raptures of this juice have come, as 'twere to heaven. to thee.
Chapter I · Hymn 22.2
Indra, victorious, Mitra-like, smote, like a Yati, Vritra dead. As Bhrigu quelled his foes, he cleft Vala in Soma's rapturous joy.
Chapter I · Hymn 22.3
Winner of gold and gear and cattle flow thou on, set as impregner, Indu! 'mid the worlds of life! Rich in brave men art thou, Soma, who winnest all: these holy singers wait upon thee with song.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.1
O Soma, thou beholdest men from every side: O Pavamana, Steer, thou wanderest through these. Pour out upon us wealth in treasure and in gold: may we have strength to live among the things that be!
Chapter II · Hymn 1.2

Thou passest to these worlds as sovran Lord thereof, O Indu, harnessing thy tawny well-winged mares. May they pour forth for thee milk and oil rich in sweets: O Soma, let the folk abide in thy decree!
Chapter II · Hymn 1.3
The streams of Pavamana, thine, finder of all I have been effused, Even as Surya's rays of light.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.1
Making the light that shines from heaven thou flowest on to every form, Soma, thou swellest like a sea.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.2
Shown forth thou sendest out thy voice, O Pavamana, with a roar. Like Surya, God, as Law commands.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.3
Hitherward have the Somas streamed, the drops while they are purified: When blent, in waters they are raised.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.1
The milk hath run to meet them like floods rushing down a precipice: They come to Indra, being cleansed.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.2
O Soma Pavamana, thou flowest as Indra's gladdener: The men have seized and lead thee forth.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.3
Thou, Indu, when, expressed by stones, thou runnest to the filter, art Ready for Indra's high decree.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.4
Victorious, to be hailed with joy, O Soma, flow delighting men, As the supporter of mankind!
Chapter II · Hymn 3.5
Flow on, best Vritra-slayer; flow meet to be hailed with joyful lauds, pure, purifying, wonderful
Chapter II · Hymn 3.6
Pure, purifying, is he called, Soma effused and full of sweets, Slayer of sinners, dear to Gods.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.7
The Sage hath robed him in the sheep's wool for the banquet of the Gods, Subduing all our enemies.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.1
For he, as Pavamana, sends thousandfold riches in the shape Of cattle to the worshippers.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.2
Thou graspest all things with thy mind, and purifiest thee with thoughts: As such, O Soma, find us fame!
Chapter II · Hymn 4.3
Pour on us lofty glory, send sure riches to our liberal lords: Bring food to those who sing thy praise!
Chapter II · Hymn 4.4
As thou art cleansed, O wondrous steed, O Soma, thou hast entered, like A pious king, into the songs,
Chapter II · Hymn 4.5
He, Soma, like a courser in the floods invincible, made bright With hands, is resting in the press.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.6
Disporting, like a liberal chief, thou goest. Soma to the sieve, Lending the laud heroic strength.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.7
Pour on us with thy juice all kinds of corn, each sort of nourishment! And, Soma, all felicities!
Chapter II · Hymn 5.1
As thine, O Indu, is the praise, and thine what springeth from, the juice, Seat thee on the dear sacred grass!
Chapter II · Hymn 5.2
And, finding for us steeds and kine, O Soma, with thy juice flow on Through days that fly most rapidly!
Chapter II · Hymn 5.3
As one who conquers, ne'er subdued, attacks and slays the enemy, Thus, vanquisher of thousands! flow!
Chapter II · Hymn 5.4
Thou, Indu, with thy streams that drop sweet juices, which were poured for help, Hast settled in the cleansing sieve.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.1
So flow thou onward through the fleece, for Indra flow to be his drink, Seating thee in the shrine of Law!
Chapter II · Hymn 6.2
As giving room and freedom, as most sweet, pour butter forth and milk, O Soma, for the Angirasas!
Chapter II · Hymn 6.3

Thy glories are, like lightnings from the rainy cloud, visible, Agni, like the comings of the Dawns, When, loosed to wander over plants and forest trees, thou crammest by thyself thy food into thy mouth.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.1

When, sped and urged by wind, thou spreadest thee abroad, soon piercing through thy food according to thy will, The hosts, who ne'er decayest, eager to consume, like men on chariots, Agni! strive on every side.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.2

Agni, the Hotar-priest who fills the assembly full, waker of wisdom, chief controller of the thought- Thee, yea, none other than thyself, doth man elect priest of the holy offering, great and small, alike.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.3
Even far and wide, O Varuna and Mitra, doth your help extend: May I obtain your kind good-will!
Chapter II · Hymn 8.1
True Gods, may we completely gain food and a dwelling place from you: Ye Mitras, may we be your own!
Chapter II · Hymn 8.2
Guard us, ye Mitras, with your guards, save us, ye skilled to save: may we Subdue the Dasyus by ourselves!
Chapter II · Hymn 8.3
Arising in thy might, thy jaws thou shookest Indra, having drunk The Soma which the press had shed.
Chapter II · Hymn 9.1
Indra, both world gave place to thee as thou wast fighting, when thou wast The slayer of the Dasyu hosts.
Chapter II · Hymn 9.2
From Indra, have I measured out a song eight-footed with nine parts, Delicate, strengthening the Law.
Chapter II · Hymn 9.3
Indra and Agni, these our songs of praise have sounded forth to you: Ye who bring blessings! drink the juice
Chapter II · Hymn 10.1
Come, Indra, Agni, with those teams, desired of many, which ye have, O heroes, for the worshipper
Chapter II · Hymn 10.2
With those to his libation poured, ye heroes, Indra, Agni, come: Come ye to drink the Soma-juice!
Chapter II · Hymn 10.3
Soma, flow on exceeding bright with loud roar to the reservoirs, Resting in wooden vats thy home!
Chapter II · Hymn 11.1
Let water winning Somas flow to Indra, Vayu, Varuna, To Vishnu and Marut host!
Chapter II · Hymn 11.2
Soma, bestowing food upon our progeny, from every side Pour on us riches thousandfold.
Chapter II · Hymn 11.3
Pressed out by pressers Soma goes over the fleecy backs of sheep, Goes even as with a mare in tawny-coloured stream, goes in a sweetly-sounding stream.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.1
Down to the water Soma, rich in kine, bath flowed with cows, with cows that have been milked. They have approached the mixing-vessels as a sea: the cheerer streams for the carouse.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.2
O Purifying Soma, bring to us the wondrous treasure, meet. For lauds, that is in earth and heaven!
Chapter II · Hymn 13.1
Cleansing the lives of men, thou, Steer, bellowing on the sacred grass, Gold-hued, hast settled in thy home.
Chapter II · Hymn 13.2
For ye twain, Indra, Soma, are Lords of heaven's light, Lords of the kine: Prosper, as mighty ones, our prayers
Chapter II · Hymn 13.3
By men hath Indra been advanced, the Vritra-sIayer, to joy and strength. Him only we invoke for help in battles whether great or small be he our aid in deeds or might!
Chapter II · Hymn 14.1
For, hero, thou art like a host, art giver of abundant spoil. Strengthening e'en the feeble, thou aidest the sacrificer, thou givest great wealth to him who pours.
Chapter II · Hymn 14.2
When war and battles are on foot, booty is offered to the bold. Yoke thou thy wildly-rushing bays! Whom wilt thou slay, and whom enrich? Do thou, O Indra, make us rich!
Chapter II · Hymn 14.3
The juice of Soma thus diffused, sweet to the taste, the bright cows drink, Who travelling in splendour close to mighty Indra's side rejoice, good in their own supremacy.
Chapter II · Hymn 15.1
Craving his touch the dappled kine mingle the Soma with their milk. The milch-kine dear to Indra send forth his death dealing thunder-bolt, good in their own supremacy.
Chapter II · Hymn 15.2
With veneration, passing wise, they honour his victorious might. They follow close his many laws to win them due preeminence, good in their own supremacy.
Chapter II · Hymn 15.3
Strong, mountain-born, the stalk hath been pressed in the streams for rapturous joy. Hawk-like he settles in his home.
Chapter II · Hymn 16.1
Fair is the juice beloved of Gods, washed in the waters, pressed by men: The milch kine sweeten it with milk
Chapter II · Hymn 16.2
Then, like a steed, have they adorned the inciter for eternal life, The meath's juice at the festival.
Chapter II · Hymn 16.3
Make high and splendid glory shine hitherward, Lord of food, God, on the friend of Gods Unclose the cask of middle air
Chapter II · Hymn 17.1
Roll onward from the press, O mighty one, effused, as kings, supporter of the tribes Pour on us rain from heaven, send us the water's flow, urging our thoughts to win the spoil!
Chapter II · Hymn 17.2
Breath of the mighty Dames, the Child, speeding the plan of sacrifice, Surpasses all things that are dear, yea, from of old.
Chapter II · Hymn 18.1
The place that is concealed hath gained a share of Trita's pressing-stones, By the seven laws of sacrifice, even that dear place.
Chapter II · Hymn 18.2
He hath sent forth unto the heights the three, in stream, as Trita's wealth: He who is passing wise measures his pathways out.
Chapter II · Hymn 18.3
Flow to the filter with thy stream, effused, to win us spoil and wealth, Soma exceeding rich in meath for Indra, Vishnu, and the Gods
Chapter II · Hymn 19.1
The hymns that know not guile, caress thee, golden-coloured, in the sieve. As mothers, Pavamana, lick the new-born calf, as Law commands.
Chapter II · Hymn 19.2
Lord of great sway, thou liftest thee above the heavens, above the earth. Thou, of Pavamana, hast assumed thy coat of mail with majesty.
Chapter II · Hymn 19.3
Strong Indu, bathed in milk, flows on for Indra, Soma exciting strength, for his carousal. He quells malignity and slays the demons, King of the homestead, he who gives us comfort.
Chapter II · Hymn 20.1
Then in a stream he flows, milked out with press-stones, mingled with sweetness, through the fleecy filter-- Indu rejoicing in the love of Indra, the God who gladdens for the God's enjoyment.
Chapter II · Hymn 20.2
He flows, as he is cleansed, to sacred duties, a God bedewing Gods with his own juices. Indu hath, clothed in powers that suit the season, on the raised fleece engaged the ten swift fingers.
Chapter II · Hymn 20.3
O Agni, God, we kindle thee, refulgent, wasting not away, That this more glorious fuel may send forth for thee its shine to heaven. Bring food to those who sing thy praise!
Chapter II · Hymn 21.1
To thee the splendid, Lord of light! bright! wondrous! prince of men! is brought. Oblation with the holy verse, O Agni, bearer of our gifts! Bring food to those who sing thy praise!
Chapter II · Hymn 21.2
Thou heatest both the ladles in thy mouth, O brilliant prince of men! So fill us also in our hymns abundantly, thou Lord of Strength. Bring food to those who sing thy praise!
Chapter II · Hymn 21.3
Sing ye a psalm to Indra; sing a great song to the lofty Sage, To him who maketh prayer, inspired, who loveth laud.
Chapter II · Hymn 22.1
Thou, Indra, art the conqueror: thou gavest splendour to the Sun. Maker of all things, thou art mighty and All-God.
Chapter II · Hymn 22.2
Radiant with light thou wentest to the sky, the luminous realm of -heaven. The Gods, O Indra, strove to win thy friendly love.
Chapter II · Hymn 22.3
This Soma hath been pressed for thee, O Indra, bold one, mightiest, come! May Indra vigour fill thee full, as Surya fills mid-air with rays
Chapter II · Hymn 23.1
Slayer of Vritra, mount thy car! The bay steeds have been yoked by prayer. May, with its voice, the pressing-stone draw thine attention hitherward!
Chapter II · Hymn 23.2
His pair of tawny coursers bring Indra, resistless in his might. Hither to Rishis' songs of praise and sacrifice performed by men.
Chapter II · Hymn 23.3
4: Light of the sacrifice, be pours delicious meathp most wealthy, father and begetter of the Gods. He, gladdening, best of cheerers, juice that Indra loves, enriches with mysterious treasure earth and heaven.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.1

The Lord of heaven, the vigorous and far-seeing one, flowsshouting to the beaker with his thousand streams. Coloured like gold he rests in seats where Mitra dwells, the Steer made beautiful by rivers and by sheep.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.2
As Pavamana thou flowest before the streams: thou goest on, before the hymn, before the kine. Thou sharest mighty booty in the van of war Soma, well-armed, thou art pressed out by men who press.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.3
Through our desire of heroes, kine, and horses, vigorous Somadrops, Brilliant and swift, have been effused.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.1
They, beautified by holy men and purified in both the hands, Are flowing through the fleecy cloth.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.2
These Soma juices shall pour forth all treasures for the worshipper, From heaven and earth and firmament.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.3
Flow, Soma, Indu, dear to Gods, swift through the purifying sieve, And enter fndra in thy strength
Chapter I · Hymn 3.1
As mighty food speed hitherward, Indu, as a most splendid steer: Sit in thy place as one with power
Chapter I · Hymn 3.2
The well-loved meath was made to flow, the stream of the creative juice: The Sage drew waters to himself.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.3
The mighty waters, yea, the floods accompany thee mighty one, When thou wilt clothe thee with the milk.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.4
The lake is brightened in the floods. Soma, our friend, heaven's prop and stay, Falls on the purifying cloth.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.5
The tawny Bull hath bellowed. fair as mighty Mitra to behold He gleams and flashes with the Sun.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.6
Songs, Indra, active in their might, are beautified for thee, wherewith Thou deckest thee for rapturous joy.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.7
To thee who givest ample room we pray, to win the wild delight, That Thou mayst have exalted praise,
Chapter I · Hymn 3.8
Winner of kine Indu, art thou, winner of heroes, steeds, and spoil: Primeval soul of sacrifice.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.9
Pour on us, Indu! Indra-strength with a full stream of sweetness, like Parianya, sender of the rain!
Chapter I · Hymn 3.10
O Soma Pavamana, be victorious, win us high renown; And make us better than we are!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.1
Win thou the light, win heavenly light, and, Soma, all felicities; And make us better than we are!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.2
Win skilful strength and mental power! O Soma, drive away our foes; And make us better than we are!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.3
Ye purifiers, purify Soma for Indra, for his drink; Make thou us better than we are!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.4
Give us our portion in the Sun through thine own mental power and aids; And make us better than we are!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.5
Through thine own mental power and aids long may we look upon the Sun: Make thou us better than we are!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.6
Well-weaponed Soma, pour to us a stream of riches doubly great; And make us better than we are!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.7
As one victorious unsubdued in battle, pour forth wealth to us: And make us better than we are!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.8
With offerings, Pavamana! men have strengthened thee as Law commands: Make thou us better than we are!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.9
O Indu, bring us wealth in steeds brilliant and quickening all life; And make us better than we are!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.10
Swift runs this giver of delight, even the stream of flowing juice: Swift runs this giver of delight.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.1
The Morning knows all precious things, the Goddess knows her grace to man: Swift runs this giver of delight.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.2
We have accepted thousands from Dhvasra's and Purusbanti's hands: Swift runs this giver of delight.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.3
From whom we have accepted thus thousands and three-times ten besides: Swift runs this giver of delight.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.4
Forth with his stream who gladdens best these Soma juices have been poured, Lauded with songs for mighty strength.
Chapter I · Hymn 6.1
Thou flowest to enjoy the milk, and bringest valour, being, cleansed: Winning the spoil flow hitherward
Chapter I · Hymn 6.2
And, hymned by Jamadagni, let all nourishment that kine supply, And general praises, flow to us!
Chapter I · Hymn 6.3
For Jatavedas, worthy of our praise, will we frame with our mind this eulogy as 'twere a car. For good, in his assembly, is this care of ours. Let us not, in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm!
Chapter I · Hymn 7.1
We will bring fuel and prepare our sacred gifts, reminding thee at each successive holy time. Fulfil our thoughts that we may lengthen out our lives Let us not, in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm!
Chapter I · Hymn 7.2
May we have power to kindle thee! Fulfil our prayers in thee the Gods eat the presented sacrifice. Bring hither the Adityas, for we long for them! Let us not, in thy friendship, Agni, suffer harm!
Chapter I · Hymn 7.3
Soon as the Sun hath risen I sing to you, to Mitra, Varuna, And Aryaman who slays the foe.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.1
With wealth of gold may this my song bring unmolested might; may this, Sages! obtain the sacrifice!
Chapter I · Hymn 8.2
May we be thine, God Varuna, and with our princes, Mitra, thine: May we gain food and heavenly light!
Chapter I · Hymn 8.3
Drive all our enemies away, smite down the foes who press around, And bring the wealth for which we long:
Chapter I · Hymn 9.1
Of which the world shall know forthwith as given by thee abundantly: Bring us the wealth for which we long:
Chapter I · Hymn 9.2
O Indra, that which is concealed in strong firm place precipito us: Bring us the wealth for which we long!
Chapter I · Hymn 9.3
Yea, ye are priests of sacrifice, winners in war and holy works Indra and Agni, mark this well!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.1
Bountiful, riders on the car, slayers of Vritra unsubdued, Indra and Agni, mark this well!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.2
The men with pressing-stones have pressed this meath of yours which gives delight: Indra and Agni, mark this well!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.3
For Indra girt by Maruts, flow, thou Indu, very rich in meath, To seat thee in the place of song!
Chapter I · Hymn 11.1
Sage: who know the lore of speech deck thee, the strong sustainer, well: Men make thee bright and beautiful.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.2
Let Mitra, Varuna, Aryaman drink Pavamana's juice, yea, thine. Sage! let the Maruts drink thereof.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.3
Deft-handed! thou when purified liftest thy voice amid the sea. Thou, Pavamana makest riches flow to us, yellow, abundant, much-desired.
Chapter I · Hymn 12.1
Made pure, as Pavamana, in the sheep's long wool, the Steer bath bellowed in the vat. Thou flowest, Soma Pavamana! balmed with 'milk unto the meeting-place of Gods.
Chapter I · Hymn 12.2
Him here, the offspring of the sea, the ten swift fingers beautify: With the Adityas is he seen.
Chapter I · Hymn 13.1
With Indra and with Vayu he, effused, flows onward with the beams Of Surya to the cleansing sieve.
Chapter I · Hymn 13.2
Flow rich in sweets and lovely for our Bhaga, Vayu, Pushan, fair For Mitra and for Varuna!
Chapter I · Hymn 13.3
With Indra splendid feasts be ours, rich in all strengthening things, wherewith, Wealthy in food, we may rejoice!
Chapter I · Hymn 14.1
Like thee, thyself, for singers yoked, thou movest, as it were besought, Bold one, the axle of the car,
Chapter I · Hymn 14.2
That, Satakratu, thou, to serve and please thy praisers, as it were, Stirrest the axle with thy strength.
Chapter I · Hymn 14.3
As a good cow to him who milks, we call the doer of good deeds, To our assistance day by day.
Chapter I · Hymn 15.1
Come thou to our libations, drink of Soma, Soma-drinker! yea, The rich one's rapture giveth kine.
Chapter I · Hymn 15.2
So may we be acquainted with thine innermost benevolence: Neglect us not; come hitherward!
Chapter I · Hymn 15.3

As, like the Morning, thou has filled, O Indra, both the earth and heaven, So as the mighty one, great King of all the mighty race of men, the Goddess mother brought thee forth, the blessed mother gave thee life.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.1

Thou bearest in thine hand a lance like a long hook, great counsellor. As with his foremost foot a goat, draw down the branch O Maghavan. The Goddess mother brought thee forth, the blessed mother gave thee life.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.2

Relax that mortal's stubborn strength whose heart is bent on wickedness. Trample him down beneath thy feet who watches for and aims at us. The Goddess mother brought thee forth, the blessed mother gave thee life.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.3
Soma, the dweller on the hills, effused, hath flowed into the sieve. All-bounteous art thou in carouse.
Chapter I · Hymn 17.1
Thou art a holy bard, a Sage; the meath offspring of thy sap: All bounteous art thou in carouse.
Chapter I · Hymn 17.2
All-d6ties of one accorcl have come that they may drink of thee: All-bounteous art thou in carouse.
Chapter I · Hymn 17.3
Effused is he who brings good things, who brings us store of wealth, and sweet refreshing food, Soma who brings us quiet homes:
Chapter I · Hymn 18.1
He whom our Indra and the Marut host shall drink, Bhaga shall drink with Aryaman, By whom we bring to us Mitra and Varuna, and Indra for our great defence.
Chapter I · Hymn 18.2
Friends, hymn your Lord who makes him pure for rapturous carouse: let them Sweeten him, as a child, with lauds and sacred gifts
Chapter I · Hymn 19.1
Like as a calf with mother cows, so Indu is urged forth and sent, Glorified by our hymns;, the god-delighting juice.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.2
Effectual help to power is he. he is a banquet for the troop, He who hath been effused, more rich in meath, for Gods.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.3
For us the Soma juices flow, the drops best furtherers of weal, Effused as friends, without a spot, benevolent, finders of the light.
Chapter I · Hymn 20.1
These Soma juices, skill.ed in song, purified, blent with milk and curd, Hastening on and firmly set in oil resemble beauteous suns.
Chapter I · Hymn 20.2
Effused by means of pressing- stones, upon the oxhide visible, They, treasure-finders, have announced food unto us from every side.
Chapter I · Hymn 20.3
Pour forth this wealth with this purification: flow onward to the yellow lake, O Indu! Here, too, the bright one, wind-swift, full of wisdom, shall give a son to him who cometh quickly.
Chapter I · Hymn 21.1
Flow on for us with this purification to the famed ford of thee whose due is glory! May the foe-queller shake us down, for triumph, like a tree's ripe fruit, sixty thousand treasures!
Chapter I · Hymn 21.2
Eagerly do we pray for those two exploits, at the blue lake and Prisana, wrought in battle. He sent our enemies to sleep and slew them, and turned away the foolish and unfriendly.
Chapter I · Hymn 21.3
O Agni, be our nearest friend, yea, our protector and our kind deliverer!
Chapter I · Hymn 22.1
As gracious Agni, famed for treasures, come, and, most resplendent, give us store of wealth!
Chapter I · Hymn 22.2
To thee then, O most bright, O radiant God, we come with prayer for happiness for our friends.
Chapter I · Hymn 22.3
May we, with Indra and the Gods to aid us, bring these existing worlds to full completion!
Chapter I · Hymn 23.1
Our sacrifice, our bodies, and our offspring, let Indra with the Adityas-form and finish!
Chapter I · Hymn 23.2
With the Adityas, with the band of Maruts, let Indra send us medicines to heal us!
Chapter I · Hymn 23.3
Sing to your Indra, mightiest Vritra-slayer, sing to the Sage the song that he accepteth!
Chapter I · Hymn 24.1
The God declares the deities' generations, like Usana, proclaiming lofty wisdom. With brilliant kin far-ruling, sanctifying, the wild boar, singing with his foot, advances.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.1
The swans, the Vrishagnas from anear us, restless, have brought their clamour to our dwelling-- Friends come to Pavamana, meet for praises-and sound in concert their resistless music.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.2
He takes the swiftness of the great Far strider: cows low as, 'twere to him who sports at pleasure. He with the sharpened horns brings forth abundance: the silvery shines by night, by day the golden.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.3
Like cars that thunder on their way, like coursers eager for renown, Have Soma drops flowed forth for wealth.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.4
Forth have they rushed from holding hands, like chariots that are urged to speed, Like joyful songs of singing-men.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.5
The Somas deck themselves with milk as kings are graced with eulogies, And, with seven priests, the sacrifice.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.6
Pressed for the gladdening draught the drops flow forth abundantly with song, Flow with the stream of savoury juice.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.7
Winning Vivasvan's glory and speeding the light of Dawn, the suns, Pass through the openings of the cloth.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.8
The singing-men of ancient time open the doors of sacred songs-- The men who bring the mighty One.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.9
In close society have come the priests, the sevenfold brotherhood, Filling the station of the One.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.10
He makes us kin with Gods, he joins the Sun, for seeing, with mine eye; I milk the Sage's offspring forth.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.11
The Sun beholdeth with his eye the heaven's dear quarter which the priests Have set within the sacred cell.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.12
Forth on their way the glorious drops have flowed for maintenance of Law, Knowing what suits this worshipper.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.1
Down in the mighty waters sinks the stream of Meath, most excellent, Oblation best of all in worth.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.2
About the holy place the Steer, true, guileless, noblest, hath sent forth, Continuous voices in the wood.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.3
When the Sage, purging manly deeds and lofty wisdom flows, around,
Chapter II · Hymn 2.4
When purified, he sits enthroned as King over the warring clans. What time the sages speed him on.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.5
Most dear, gold-coloured, in the fleece he sinks, and settles in the wood: The singer is besieged with song.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.6
He goes to Indra, Vayu, and the Asvins with the rapturous joy, To whomsoe'er his power delights.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.7
The waves of pleasant Soma flow to Bhaga, Mitra, Varuna, Well knowing, through his mighty powers.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.8
Gain for us, O ye Heaven and Earth, riches of Meath to win us strength: Gain for us treasures and renown.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.9
We choose to-day that chariot-steed of thine, the strong, that brings us bliss, The guardian, the desire of all;
Chapter II · Hymn 2.10
The excellent, the gladdener, the Sage with heart that understands. The guardian, the desire of all;
Chapter II · Hymn 2.11
Who for ourselves, O thou most wise, is wealth and fair intelligence, The guardian, the desire of all.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.12
Agni Vaisvanara, born in course of Order, the messenger of earth, the head of heaven, The Sage, the Sovran, guest of men, our vessel fit for their mouth, the Gods have generated.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.1
To thee, immortal! when to life thou springest all the Gods sing for joy as to their infant. They by thy mental powers were made immortal, Vaisvdnara when thou shonest from thy parents.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.2
Him have they praised, mid-point of sacrifices, great cistern of libations, seat of riches. Vaisvanara, conveyer of oblations, ensign of worship, have the Gods engendered.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.3
Sing forth unto your Varuna and Mitra with a song inspired: They, mighty Lords, are lofty law.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.1
Full springs of fatness, sovran Kings, Mitra and Varuna, the twain, Gods glorified among the Gods,
Chapter II · Hymn 4.2
So help ye us to riches, great celestial and terrestrial wealth! Vast is your sway among the Gods.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.3
O Indra marvellously bright, come, these libations long for thee, Thus by firie fingers purified!
Chapter II · Hymn 5.1
Urged by the holy singer, sped by song, come nigb, O Indra, to The sacrificing suppliant's pravers!
Chapter II · Hymn 5.2
Approach, O Indra, basting thee, Lord of bay horses, to our prayers: In our libation t ake delight!
Chapter II · Hymn 5.3
Glorify him who compasses all forests with his glowing Dame, And leaves them blackened by his tongue.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.1
He who gains Indra's grace by fire enkindled, finds as easy way Over the floods to splendid wealth.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.2
Give us, ye twain, swift steeds to bring Indra and Agni, and bestow Abundant food with wealth on us.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.3

Indu hath started forth for Indra's settled place, and slights not,. as a friend, the promise of his friend. Soma comes onward like a youth with youthful maids, and gains the beaker by a course of hundred paths.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.1

Your hymns of pleasant sound, praiseworthy, fond of lauds, have come into the hall enclosed for sacrifice. Singers have hymned the golden-coloured as he sports, and milchkine have come near to meet him with their milk,
Chapter II · Hymn 7.2

O Soma, Indu, while they cleanse thee, with thy wave pour orb us plentiful accumulated food, Which, ceaseless, thrice a day shall yield us hero power enriched. with store of nourishment, and strength, and meath.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.3
No one by deed attains to him who works and strengthens evermore: No, not by sacrifice, to Indra praised of all, resistless, daring, bold in might;
Chapter II · Hymn 8.1
The powerful conqueror, invincible in war, him at whose birth the mighty ones, The kine who spread afar, sent their loud voices out, heavens, earths sent their loud voices out.
Chapter II · Hymn 8.2
Sit down, O friends, and sing aloud to him who purifies himself: Deck him for glory, like a child, with holy rites
Chapter II · Hymn 9.1
Loose him who bringeth household wealth, even as a calf with. mother kine, Him who bath double strength, strong, god-delighting juice!
Chapter II · Hymn 9.2
Purify him who gives us power, most blissful one, that he may be A banquet for the troop, Mitra, and Varuna!
Chapter II · Hymn 9.3
The Strong hath flowed forth in a thousand streams, flowed through the filter and the sheep's long wool.
Chapter II · Hymn 10.1
With ceaseless genial flow the Strong hath run, purified by the waters, blent with milk.
Chapter II · Hymn 10.2
Pressed out with stones, directed by the men, go forth, O Soma, into Indra's throat!
Chapter II · Hymn 10.3
The Soma juices which have been expressed afar or near at hand, Or there on Saryanavan's bank,
Chapter II · Hymn 11.1
Those pressed among Arjikas, pressed among the active, in, men's homes, Or pressed among the Fivefold Tribes--
Chapter II · Hymn 11.2
May these celestial drops, expressed, pour forth upon us, as they flow, Rain from the heavens and hero strength!
Chapter II · Hymn 11.3
May Vatsa draw thy mind away even from thy loftiest dwelling-place! Agni, I yearn for thee with song.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.1
Thou art alike in many a place: through all the regions thou art Lord. In fray and fight we call on thee.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.2
When we are seeking spoil we call Agni to help us in the strife, Giver of wordrous gifts in war.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.3
O Indra, bring great strength to us, bring valour, 5atakratu, thou most active, bring A hero conquering in war!
Chapter II · Hymn 13.1
For, gracious Satakratu, thou hast ever been a mother and a sire to us, So now for bliss we pray to thee.
Chapter II · Hymn 13.2
To thee, strong! much-invoked! who showest forth thy strength, made very mighty! do I speak: So grant thou us heroic power!
Chapter II · Hymn 13.3
Stone-Darting Indra, wonderous God, what wealth thou hast not given me here, That bounty, treasure-finder! bring, filling full both thy hands, to us!
Chapter II · Hymn 14.1
Bring what thou deemest worth the wish, O Indra that which is in heavem! So may we know thee as thou art a giver boundless in thy gifts!
Chapter II · Hymn 14.2
Thy lofty spirit famed in all the regions as appeasable,-- With this thou rendest even things firm, Stone-darter! so to win thee strength.
Chapter II · Hymn 14.3
5: The Maruts with their troop adorn and brighten, even at his birth, the Sage, the lovely infant. By songs a poet, and a Sage by wisdom, Soma goes singing through the cleansing filter.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.1
Light-winner, Rishi-minded, Rishi-maker, hymned in a thousand hymns, leader of sages, Eager to gain his third form, mighty, Soma is, like Viraj, resplendent as a singer.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.2
Hawk seated in the press, bird wide-extended, the banner seeking kine and wielding weapons, Uniting with the sea, the wave of waters, the mighty tells his fourth form and declares it.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.3
Obeying Indra's dear desire these Soma juices have flowed forth Increasing his heroic might.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.1
Laid in the press and flowing pure to Vayu and the Asvins, may These give us great heroic strength.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.2
Soma, as thou art purified, incite to bounty Indra's heart, To seat him in the shrine of Gods!
Chapter I · Hymn 2.3
The ten swift fingers deck thee forth seven ministers impel thee on, The sages have rejoiced in thee.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.4
When through the filter thou art poured we clothe thee with a robe of milk, To be a rapturous feast for Gods.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.5
When purified within the jars, Soma bright-red and golden-hued, Hath veiled him in a milky dress.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.6
Flow onward to our wealthy lords. Drive all our enemies away: O lndu, pass into thy friend!
Chapter I · Hymn 2.7
May we obtain thee, Indra's drink, who viewest men and findest light, Gain thee and progeny and food!
Chapter I · Hymn 2.8
Send down the rain from heaven and make splendour upon the earth! Give us, O Soma, victory in war!
Chapter I · Hymn 2.9
Poured through the fleece in thousand streams purified Soma floweth to, Indra's and Vayu's meeting-place.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.1
Sing forth, ye men who long for help, to Pavamana, to the Sage, Effused to entertain the Gods!
Chapter I · Hymn 3.2
The Soma drops with thousand powers are purified to win us strength, Hymned to become the feast of Gods.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.3
Yea, as thou flowest bring great store of food that we may win us strength: Indu, bring splendid manly might
Chapter I · Hymn 3.4
Like coursers by their drivers urged, they were poured forth, to win us strength, Swift through the woollen straining-cloth.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.5
May they in flowing give us wealth in thousands, and heroic power,-- These godlike Soma drops effused!
Chapter I · Hymn 3.6
The roaring Soma drops flow on, like milch-kine lowing to, their calves: They have run forth from both the hands.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.7
Beloved by Indra, bringing joy, roaring as thou art purified, Drive all our enemies away.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.8
As Pavamanas, driving off the godless, looking on the light, Sit in the place of sacrifice.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.9
The Soma drops, exceeding rich in sweets, to Indra have been poured, Shed with the stream of sacrifice.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.1
Sages have called to Indra, like cows, milch-kine, lowing to their calves, Called him to drink the Soma juice.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.2
In the stream's wave wise Soma dwells, distilling rapture, in his. seat, Resting upon a wild cow's hide.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.3
Far-sighted Soma, Sage and bard, is worshipped in the central point, Of heaven, the straining-cloth of wool.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.4
In close embracement Indu holds Soma when poured within the: jars. And on the purifying sieve.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.5
Indu sends forth a voice on high, up in the region of the sea. Stirring the cask that drops with meath.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.6
The tree whose praises never fail dwells in the stream of holy milk, Urged onward by its human friend.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.7
O Pavamana bring us wealth bright with a thousand splendours; yea, O Indu, give us ready help!
Chapter I · Hymn 4.8
Sage, poet, poured with all his stream, Soma is driven, far away, To the dear places of the sky.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.9
Loud as a river's roaring wave thy powers have lifted up themselves: Urge on thine arrow's sharpened point!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.1
At thine effusion upward rise three voices fresh and strong, when thou. Flowest upon the fleecy ridge.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.2
On to the fleece they urge with stones the dear, the goldencoloured one, Even Pavamana dropping meath.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.3
Flow with thy current to the sieve, O Sage, best giver of delight, To seat these in the shrine of song!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.4
Best giver of delight, flow on anointed with the milk for balm, And enter into Indra's throat!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.5
Flow onward, Indu, with this food for him who in thy wild delights, Battered the nine-and-ninety down.
Chapter I · Hymn 6.1
Smote swiftly forts, and Sambara, then Yadu and that Turvasa, For pious Divodasa's sake!
Chapter I · Hymn 6.2
Finder of horses, pour on us horses and wealth in kine and gold, And Indu, food in boundless store!
Chapter I · Hymn 6.3
Chasing our foemen, driving off the godless, Soma floweth on, Going to Indra's settled place.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.1
O Pavamana, hither bring great riches, and destroy our foes: O Indu, grant heroic fame!
Chapter I · Hymn 7.2
A hundred obstacles have ne'er checked thee when rain to give thy boons, When, being cleansed, thou combatest.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.3
Flow onward with that stream wherewith thou gavest splendour to the sun, Speeding the waters kind to man!
Chapter I · Hymn 8.1
He, Pavamana, high o'er man, yoked the Sun's courser Etasa, To travel through the realm of air.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.2
Yea, those bay steeds he harnessed to the chariot that the Sun might come: Indu, he said, is Indra's self.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.3
Associate with fires, make your God Agni envoy at sacrifice, best skilled in worship, Established firm among mankind, the holy flame-crowned and fed with oil, the purifier!
Chapter I · Hymn 9.1

Like a steed neighing eager for the pasture, when he hath stepped forth from the great enclosure: Then the wind following blows upon his splendour, and, straight, the path is black which thou hast travelled.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.2
From thee, a bull but newly born, O Agni, the kindled everlasting flames rise upward. Aloft to heaven as ruddy smoke thou mountest: Agni, thou speedest to the Gods as envoy.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.3
We make this Indra very strong to strike the mighty Vritra dead: A vigorous hero shall he be.
Chapter I · Hymn 10.1
This Indra, made for giving gifts, is stablished, mightiest, in strength, Bright, meet for Soma, famed in song.
Chapter I · Hymn 10.2
By song, as 'twere' the powerful bolt which none may parry, was prepared: Strong and invincible he grew.
Chapter I · Hymn 10.3
Adhvaryu, to the filter lead the Soma juice expressed with stones: Make thou it pure for Indra's drink!
Chapter I · Hymn 11.1
These Gods and all the Marut host, Indu! enjoy this juice of thine, This Pavamana's flowing meath.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.2
Pour out for Indra, Thunder-armed, the milk of heaven, the Soma's juice, Most excellent, most rich in sweets!
Chapter I · Hymn 11.3

On flows the potent juice, sustainer of the heavens, the strength of Gods, whom men must hail with shouts of joy, Thou, gold-hued, started like a courser by brave men, art lightly showing forth thy splendour in the streams.
Chapter I · Hymn 12.1

He takes his weapons, like a hero, in his hands, fain to win light, car-borne, in forays for the kine. Indu, while stimulating Indra's might, is urged forward and balmed by sages skilful in their task.
Chapter I · Hymn 12.2

Soma, as thou art purified with flowing wave, exhibiting thy strength enter thou Indra's throat. Make both worlds stream for us, as lightning doth the clouds: mete out exhaustless powers for us through this our prayer!
Chapter I · Hymn 12.3
