Though, Indra, thou art called by men eastward and westward, north and south, Thou chiefly art with Anava and Turvasa, brave champion! urged by men to come.
Chapter I · Hymn 13.1
Or, Indra, when with Ruma, Rusama, Syavaka, and Kripa thou rejoicest thee, Still do the Kanvas, bringing prayer, with hymns of praise O Indra, draw thee hither: come!
Chapter I · Hymn 13.2
Both boons,-may, Indra, hitherward turned, listen to this prayer of ours. And mightiest Maghavan with thought inclined to us come near to drink to Soma juice!
Chapter I · Hymn 14.1
For him, strong, independent ruler, Heaven and Earth have fashioned forth with power and might. Thou seatest thee as first among thy peers in place, for thy soul longs for Soma juice.
Chapter I · Hymn 14.2
God, working with mankind flow on; to Indra go thy gladdening juice: To Vayu mount as Law commands!
Chapter I · Hymn 15.1
O Soma Pavamana, thou pourest out wealth that may be famed: O Indu, pass into the lake!
Chapter I · Hymn 15.2
Soma, thou flowest chasing foes, finder of wisdom and delight: Drive thou the godless folk afar!
Chapter I · Hymn 15.3
Stream on us riches that are craved by hundreds, best at winning spoil, Riches, O Indu, thousandfold, most splendid, that surpass the light!
Chapter I · Hymn 16.1
May we, O Vasu, be most near to this thy bounty, food, and wealth! Desired by many men, and in thy favour, O resistless one!
Chapter I · Hymn 16.2
Effused, this Indu hath flowed on, distilling rapture, to the fleece. He streams erect to sacrifice, as 'twere with splendour, seeking kine.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.3
Flow onward, Soma, as a mighty sea, as Father of the Gods, to every form!
Chapter I · Hymn 17.1
Flow on, O Soma, radiant for the Gods, blissful to heaven and earth and living things!
Chapter I · Hymn 17.2
Thou art, bright juice, sustainer of the sky: flow, mighty, in accordance with true law!
Chapter I · Hymn 17.3
I laud your most beloved guest, like a dear friend, O Agni, him! Who, like a chariot, wins us wealth.
Chapter I · Hymn 18.1
Whom as a Sage who merits praise the Gods have, from the olden time, Established among mortal men.
Chapter I · Hymn 18.2
Do thou, most youthful God, protect the men who offer, hear their songs, And of thyself preserve their seed!
Chapter I · Hymn 18.3
Come unto us, O Indra, dear, still conquering, unconcealable Wide as a mountain spread on all sides, Lord of heaven.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.1
O truthful Soma-drinker, thou art mightier than both the worlds. Thou strengthenest him who pours'libation, Lord of heaven.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.2
For thou art he, O Indra, who upholdeth all our fortresses, The Dasyu's slayer, man's sustainer, Lord of heaven.
Chapter I · Hymn 19.3
Render of forts, the young, the wise, of strength unmeasured, was he born, Sustainer of each sacred rite, Indra, the Thunderer, much extolled,
Chapter I · Hymn 20.1
Thou wielder of the stone, didst burst the cave of Vala rich in kine. The Gods came pressing to thy side, and free from terror aided thee.
Chapter I · Hymn 20.2
They glorified with hymns of praise Indra who reigneth by his might, Whose bounteous gifts in thousands come, yea, even more abundantly.
Chapter I · Hymn 20.3
Guard of all being, generating creatures, loud roared the sea as highest law commanded. Strong in the filter, on the fleecy summit, pressed from the stone, Soma hath waxen mighty.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.1
Make Vayu glad, for furtherance and bounty: cheer Varuna and Mitra, as they cleanse thee! Gladden the Gods, gladden the host of Maruts: make Heaven and Earth rejoice, O God, O Soma!
Chapter II · Hymn 1.2
Soma, the mighty, when, the water's offspring, he chose the Gods, performed that great achievement. He, Pavamana, granted strength to Indra: he, Indu, generated strength in Surya.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.3
Here present this immortal God flies, like a bird upon her wings, To settle in the vats of wood.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.1
Praised by the sacred bards, this God dives into waters, and bestows Rich gifts upon the worshipper.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.2
He. like a warrior going forth with heroes, as he flows along. Is fain to win all precious boons.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.3
This God as he is flowirig on speeds like a car and gives his aid: He lets his voice be heard of all.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.4
This God, while flowing, is adorned, gold-coloured, for the spoil, by men Devout and skilled in holy songs.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.5
This God, made ready with the hymn runs swiftly through the winding ways, Inviolable as he flows.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.6
A way he rushes with his stream, across the regions, into heaven, And roars as he is flowing on.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.7
While flowing, meet for sacrifice, he hath gone up to heaven, across The regions, never overthrown.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.8
By generation long ago, this God, engendered for the Gods, Flows tawny to the straining-cloth.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.9
This Lord of many holy laws, even at his birth engendering strength, Effused, flows onward in a stream.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.10
Through the fine fingers, with the song, this hero comes with rapid cars, Going to Indra's settled place.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.1
In holy thought he ponders much for the great service of theGods, Where the immortals have their seat.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.2
Men beautify him in the vats, him worthy to be beautified, Him who brings forth abundant food.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.3
He is deposited and led along the consecrated path When zealous men are urging him,
Chapter II · Hymn 3.4
He moves, a vigorous steed, adorned with beauteous rays of shining gold, He who is Sovran of the streams.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.5
He brandishes his horns on high, and whets them, bull who leads the herd, Doing with might heroic deeds.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.6
He, over places rough to pass bringing rich treasures, closely pressed. Descends into the reservoirs.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.7
Him, even him the golden-hued, well armed, best giver of delight, Ten fingers urge to run his course.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.8
This Bull, this chariot robes him in the sheep's long wool as heproceeds. To war that wins a thousand spoils.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.1
The dames of Trita with the stones urge forth this goldencoloured one, Indu to Indra for his drink.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.2
He like a falcon settles down amid the families of men, Like lover speeding to his love.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.3
This young exhilarating juice looks downward from its place in heaven, This Soma drop that pierced the sieve.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.4
Pressed for the draught, this tawny juice flows forth intelligent, calling out, Unto the well-beloved place.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.5
Him, here, the gold-decked skilful ten cleanse carefully, who make him bright. And beauteous for the gladdening draught.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.6
Urged by the men, this vigorous steed, Lord of the mind omniscient, Flies to the long wool of the sheep.
Chapter II · Hymn 5.1
Within the filter hath he flowed, this Soma for the Gods effused. Entering all their essences.
Chapter II · Hymn 5.2
He shines in beauty there, this God, immortal, in his dwellingplace, Foe-slayer, dearest to the Gods.
Chapter II · Hymn 5.3
Directed by the sisters ten, bellowing on his way this Steer Runs onward to the wooden vats.
Chapter II · Hymn 5.4
This Pavamana, gladdening drink within the purifying sieve, Gave splendour to the Sun in heaven.
Chapter II · Hymn 5.5
Unconquerable Lord of speech, dwelling beside Viavasvan, he Mounts up together with the Sun.
Chapter II · Hymn 5.6
This Sage, exalted by our lands, flows to the purifying sieve, Scattering foes as he is cleansed.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.1
Giver of strength, winner of light, for Indra and for Vayu he Is poured upon the filtering-cloth.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.2
The men conduct him, Soma, Steer, omniscient the head of heaven. Effused into the vats of wood.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.3
Longing for kine, longing for gold hath Indu Pavamana roared, Still conqueror, never overcome.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.4
To Indra in the firmament this mighty tawny Steer hath flowed This Indu, being purified.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.5
This Soma being purified flows mighty and invincible, Slayer of sinners, dear to Gods.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.6
This Soma, strong effused for draught, flows to the purifying sieve, Slaying the fiends, loving the Gods.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.1
Far sighted, tawny-coloured, he flows to the sieve intelligent, Bellowing to his place of rest.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.2
This vigorous Pavamana runs forth to the luminous realm of heaven, Fiend-slayer, through the sheep's long wool.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.3
This Pavamana, up above on Trita's ridge, hath made the Sun, Together with the Sisters, shine.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.4
Effused, this Soma, Steer, who slays Vritra, room-giver, unbeguiled, Hath gone as 'twere to win the spoil.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.5
Urged by the sage upon his way, this God speeds forward to the: vats, Indu to Indra, giving boons.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.6
The man who reads the essence stored by saints, the Pavamana hymns, Tastes food completely purified, made sweet by Matarisvan's touch.
Chapter II · Hymn 8.1
Whoever reads the essence stored by saints, the Pavamana hymns, For him Sarasvat! pours forth water and butter, milk and meath.
Chapter II · Hymn 8.2
Yea, for the Pavamanas flow richly, drop fatness, bring us weal,-- Amrit deposited among the Brahmans, essence stored by saints.
Chapter II · Hymn 8.3
So may the Pavamana hymns bestow on us this world and that, And gratify our hearts' desires'-the Goddesses combined with Gods!
Chapter II · Hymn 8.4
The purifying flood wherewith Gods ever purify themselves,-- With that, in thousand currents, may the Pavamanas make us clean!
Chapter II · Hymn 8.5
The Pavamana hymns bring weal: by these man goes to Paradise, And, eating pure and holy food, attains to immortality.
Chapter II · Hymn 8.6

We with great reverence have approached the Youngest, who hath shone forth well kindled in his dwelling, Wondrously bright between wide earth and heaven, well worshipped, looking forth in all directions.
Chapter II · Hymn 9.1
Through his great might o'ercoming all misfortunes, praised in the house is Agni Jatavedas. May he preserve us from disgrace and trouble, both us who laud him and our wealthy princes!
Chapter II · Hymn 9.2
O Agni, thou art Varuna and Mitra: Vasishthas! with their holy hymns exalt thee. With thee be most abundant gain of treasure! Do ye preserve us evermore with blessing!
Chapter II · Hymn 9.3
Indra, great in his power and might, and like Parjanya rich in rain. Hath been increased by Vatsa's lauds.
Chapter II · Hymn 10.1
Since Kanvas have with lauds made him completer of the sacrifice, Words are their own appropriate arms.
Chapter II · Hymn 10.2
When priests who magnify the Son of holy law present their gifts, Sages with Order's hymn of praise.
Chapter II · Hymn 10.3
Of gold-hued Pavamana, great destroyer, radiant streams have flowed, Swift streams of him whose gleams are swift.
Chapter II · Hymn 11.1
Best rider of the chariot, praised with fairest praise 'mid beauteous ones, Gold gleaming with the Marut host,
Chapter II · Hymn 11.2
Penetrate, Pavamana, best at winning booty, with thy rays, Giving the Singer hero strength!
Chapter II · Hymn 11.3
Hence sprinkle forth the juice effused, Soma, the best of sacred gifts, Who, friend of man, hath run among the water-streams He hath pressed Soma out with stones.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.1
Now, being purified, flow hither through the fleece, invincible and more odorous! We joy in thee in waters when thou art effused, blending thee still with juice and milk.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.2
Pressed out for all to see, delighting Gods, Indu, far-seeing one, is mental power.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.3

Even as a King hath Soma, red and tawny Bull, been pressed the wondrous one hath bellowed to the kine. While purified thou passest through the filtering fleece to seat thee hawk-like in the place that drops with oil.
Chapter II · Hymn 13.1

Parjanya is the sire of the leaf-bearing Bull: on mountains, in earth's centre hath he made his home. The waters have flowed forth, the Sisters, to the kine: he meets the pressing-stones at the beloved rite.
Chapter II · Hymn 13.2

To glory goest thou, a Sage with ordering skill, like a groomed steed thou rushest forward to the prize. Be gracious to us, Soma, driving off distress! Thou goest, clothed in butter, to a robe of state.
Chapter II · Hymn 13.3
Turning as 'twere to meet the Sun, enjoy from Indra all good things! When he who will be born is born with power we look to treasures as our heritage.
Chapter II · Hymn 14.1
Praise him who sends us wealth, prompt with his liberal boons Good 4re the gifts that Indra gives. He is not wroth with one who satisfies his wish: he instigates, his mind to give.
Chapter II · Hymn 14.2
Indra, give us security from that whereof we are afraid Help us, O Maghavan, let thy favour aid us thus drive away foes and enemies!
Chapter II · Hymn 15.1
For thou, O liberal Lord of ample bounty, art the ruler of our house and home. So, Indra Maghavan, thou lover of the song, we with pressed Soma call on thee.
Chapter II · Hymn 15.2
Thou, Soma, hast a running stream, sweet-toned most strong at sacrifice: Flow bounteously bestowing wealth
Chapter II · Hymn 16.1
Thou most delightful, when effused, running, the best of gladdeners, art Indu, still conquering, ne'er subdued.
Chapter II · Hymn 16.2
Do thou, poured forth by pressing- stones, flow hither uttering a roar, And bring us brightly-glorious strength!
Chapter II · Hymn 16.3
In might, O Indu, with thy streams flow for the banquet of the Gods: Rich in meath, Soma, in our beaker take thy seat!
Chapter II · Hymn 17.1
Thy drops that swim in water have exalted Indra to delight The Gods have drunk thee up for immortality.
Chapter II · Hymn 17.2
Stream opulence to us, ye drops of Soma, pressed and purified Pouring down rain from heaven in floods, and finding light!
Chapter II · Hymn 17.3
Him with the fleece they purify, brown, golden-hued beloved of all, Who with exhilarating juice goes forth to all the deities
Chapter II · Hymn 18.1
Whom, bright with native splendour, crushed between the preesing-stones, a friend. Whom Indra dearly loves, the waves and ten companions dip and bathe
Chapter II · Hymn 18.2
For Vritra-slaying Indra, thou, Soma, art poured that he may drink, And for the guerdon-giving man, the hero sitting in his seat.
Chapter II · Hymn 18.3
Flow onward Soma, flow for mighty strength, as a strong courser, bathed, to win the prize.
Chapter II · Hymn 19.1
The pressers clarify this juice of thine, the Soma for delight and lofty fame.
Chapter II · Hymn 19.2
They deck the gold-hued infant, newly-born, even Soma, Indu, in the sieve, for Gods.
Chapter II · Hymn 19.3
The Gods have come to Indu well-descended, beautified with milk, The active crusher of the foe.
Chapter II · Hymn 20.1
Even as mother cows their calf, so let our praise-songs strengthen him, Yea, him who winneth Indra's heart!
Chapter II · Hymn 20.2
Soma, pour blessings on our kine, pour forth the food that streams with milk: Increase the sea, praiseworthy one!
Chapter II · Hymn 20.3
Hitherward! they who light the flame and straightway trim the sacred grass, Whose friend is Indra ever young.
Chapter II · Hymn 21.1
Large is their fuel, much their laud, wide is their splinter from the stake, Whose friend is Indra ever young.
Chapter II · Hymn 21.2
Unquelled in fight the hero leads his army with the warrior chiefs, Whose friend is Indra ever young.
Chapter II · Hymn 21.3
He who alone bestoweth wealth on mortal man who offereth gifts, Is Indra only, potent Lord whom none resist.
Chapter II · Hymn 22.1
Whoever with the Soma pressed draws thee away from many men,- Verily Indra gains thereby tremendous power.
Chapter II · Hymn 22.2
When willhe trample, like a weed, the man who hath no gift for him? When, verily, will Indra hear our songs of praise?
Chapter II · Hymn 22.3
The singers hymn thee, they who chant the psalm of praise are lauding thee. The Brahmans have exalted thee, O Satakratu, like a pole.
Chapter II · Hymn 23.1
When thou wast climbing ridge from ridge, he looked upon the toilsome task: Indra takes notice of that wish, and the Ram hastens with his troop.
Chapter II · Hymn 23.2
Harness thy pair of strong bay steeds, long-maned, whose bodies fill the girths. And, Indra, Soma drinker, come to listen to our songs Of praise!
Chapter II · Hymn 23.3
6: Agni,well kindled bring the Gods for him who offers holy gifts; And worship them, pure Hotar-priest!
Chapter I · Hymn 1.1
O Sage, Tanunapat, present our sacrifice to Gods to-day, Sweet to the taste, that they may help!
Chapter I · Hymn 1.2
Dear Narasansa, sweet of tongue, presenter of oblations, I Invoke to this our sacrifice.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.3
Agni, on thy most easy car, entreated, hither bring the Gods! Manus-appointed Priest art thou.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.4
So when the Sun hath risen to-day may sinless Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, and Savitar send us forth!
Chapter I · Hymn 2.1
May this our home be guarded well: forward, ye bounteous, on the way, Who bear us safely o'er distress!
Chapter I · Hymn 2.2
Yea, Aditi, and those great Kings whose statute is inviolate, Are sovrans of a vast domain.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.3
Let Soma juices make thee glad! Display thy bounty, Thunderer: Drive off the enemies of prayer!
Chapter I · Hymn 3.1
Crush with thy foot the niggard churls who bring no gifts! mighty art thou: There is not one to equal thee.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.2
Thou art the Lord of Somas pressed, Somas unpressed are also thine: Thou art the Sovran of the folk.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.3
True object of our hymns, Sage, watchful Soma hath settled in the press as they refine him. Him the Adhvaryus, paired and eager, follow, leaders of sacrifice and skilful-handed.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.1
He, purified and bringing gifts to Surya, hath filled full heaven and earth, and hath disclosed them. He by whose dear help heroes gain their wishes will yield the precious meed as to a victor.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.2
He, being cleansed, the strengthener and increaser, bountiful Soma helped us his lustre, Wherein our sires of old who knew the footsteps found light and sought the kine within the mountain.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.3
Glorify naught besides, O friends, so shall no sorrow trouble you! Praise only mighty Indra, when the juice is shed, and say your lauds repeatedly!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.1
Even him, the swift one, like a bull who rushes down men's conqueror, bounteous like a cow; Him who is cause of both, of enmity and peace, to both sides most munificent.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.2
These songs of our exceeding sweet, these hymns of praise ascend to thee, Like ever-conquering chariots that display their strength, gain wealth and give unfailing help.
Chapter I · Hymn 6.1
The Bhrigus are like suns, like Kanvas, and have gained each thing whereon their thought was bent. The living men of Priyamedha's race have sun g exalting Indra with their lauds.
Chapter I · Hymn 6.2
Run forth to battle conquering the Vritras! thou Speedest to quell the foe like one exacting debts.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.1
Thou Pavamana, didst beget the Sun with might, and rain in the supporting sky, Hasting to us with plenty vivified with milk.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.2
For, Soma, we rejoice ourselves in thee effused for great supremacy in fight; Thou, Pavamana, enterest into mighty deeds.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.3
Flow forth, O Soma, flow thou onward, sweet to Indra's, Mitra's, Pushan's, Bhaga's taste!
Chapter I · Hymn 8.1
So flow thou on as bright celestial juice, flow to the vast immortal dwelling-place!
Chapter I · Hymn 8.2
Let Indra drink, O Soma, of thy juice for wisdom, and all deities for strength!
Chapter I · Hymn 8.3

Even as the beams of Surya, urging men to speed, they issue forth together, gladdening as they flow, These swift outpourings in long course of holy rites: no form save only Indra shows itself so pure.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.1

The thought is deeply fixed, the savoury juice is shed; the tongue with joyous sound is stirring in the mouth: And Pavamana, like the shout of those who press, the drop, rich in sweet juice, is flowing through the fleece.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.2

The bull is bellowing; the cows are coming nigh: the Goddesses approach the God's own resting-place. Onward hath Soma pressed through the sheep's fair bright fleece, and hath, as 'twere, endued a garment newly washed.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.3
From the two fire-sticks have the men engendered, with thought, urged by the hand, the glorious Agni, Far-seen, with pointed flame, Lord of the Homestead.
Chapter I · Hymn 10.1
The Vasus set that Agni in the dwelling, fair to behold, for help, from every quarter: Who, in the house for ever, must be honoured.
Chapter I · Hymn 10.2
Shine thou before us, Agni, well-enkindled, with flame, most youthful God, that never fadeth! To thee come goods and treasures all together.
Chapter I · Hymn 10.3
This spotted Bull hath come and sat before the mother in the east, Advancing to his father heaven.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.1
As expiration from his breath, his radiance penetrates within The Bull shines out through all the sky.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.2
Song is bestowed upon the Bird: it reigns supreme through thirty realms. Throughout the days at break of morn.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.3
Chant we a hymn to Agni while we go to sacrifice, to him Who hears us even from afar!
Chapter II · Hymn 1.1
Who from of old, in carnage, when the folk were gathered, hath preserved. His household for the worshipper.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.2
May that most blissful Agni guard our wealth and all ourfamily. And keep us safe from pain and grief
Chapter II · Hymn 1.3
Yea, let men say, Agni is born, even he who slayeth Vritra, he, Who winneth wealth in every fight!
Chapter II · Hymn 1.4
Harness, O Agni, O thou God, thy steeds which are most excellent! The fleet ones bring the rapidly.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.1
Come hither, bring the Gods to us to taste the sacrificial feast, To drink the draught of Soma juice!
Chapter II · Hymn 2.2
O Agni of the Bharatas, flame splendid with unfading might Shine forth and gleam, eternal one!
Chapter II · Hymn 2.3
Let him, as mortal, crave this speech for him who presses of the juice! As Bhrigu's sons chased Makha, so drive ye the niggard hound away.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.1
The kinsman hath endued his robe even as a son is clasped in arms. He went, as lover to a dame, to take his station suitor-like.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.2
That hero who produces strength, he who hath propped both worlds apart, Gold-hued, hath wrapped him in the sieve to settle, priest-like, in his place.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.3
Still, Indra, from all ancient time rivalless ever and companionless art thou: Thou seekest friendship but in war.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.1
Thou findest not the wealthy man to be thy friend: those scorn thee who are flown with wine. What time thou thunderest and gatherest, then thou, even as a father, art invoked.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.2
A thousand and a hundred steeds are harnessed to thy golden car: Yoked by devotion, Indra, let the long-maned bays bring thee to drink the Soma juice!
Chapter II · Hymn 5.1
Yoked to thy chariot wrought of gold, may thy two bays with, peacock tails. Convey thee hither, steeds with their white backs, to quaff sweet juice that makes us eloquent!
Chapter II · Hymn 5.2
So drink, thou lover of the song, as the first drinker, of this juice. This the outpouring of the savoury sap prepared is good and meet to gladden thee.
Chapter II · Hymn 5.3
Press ye and pour him, like a steed, laud-worthy, speeding through the region and the flood, Who swims in water, dwells in wood
Chapter II · Hymn 6.1
The Steer with thousand streams who poureth out the rain, dear to the race of deities; Who, born in Law, hath waxen mighty by the Law, King, God, and lofty ordinance.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.2
Served with oblation, kindled, bright, through love of song, may Agni, bent On riches, smite the Vritras dead
Chapter II · Hymn 7.1
His father's father, shining in his mother's ever-lasting side, Set on the seat of sacrifice!
Chapter II · Hymn 7.2
O active Jatavedas, bring devotion that wins progeny, Agni, that it may shine to heaven!
Chapter II · Hymn 7.3
Made pure by this man's urgent zeal and impulse, the God hath with his juice the Gods pervaded. Pressed, singing, to the sieve he goes, as passes the Hotar to enclosures hoiding cattle.
Chapter II · Hymn 8.1
Robed in fair raiment meet to wear in combat, a mighty Sage pronouncing invocations, Roll onward to the press-boards as they cleanse thee, far-seeing at the feast of Gods and watchful!
Chapter II · Hymn 8.2
Dear, he is brightened on the fleecy summit, a prince among us, nobler than the noble. Roar out as thou art purified, run forward! Do ye preserve us evermore with blessings!
Chapter II · Hymn 8.3
Come now and let us glorify pure Indra with pure Sama hymn! Let milk-blent juice delight him made stronger with pure, pure songs of praise!
Chapter II · Hymn 9.1
O Indra, come thou pure to us, with pure assistance pure thyself! Pure, send thou riches down to us, and, meet for Soma! pure, rejoice!
Chapter II · Hymn 9.2
O Indra, pure, vouchsafe us wealth, and, pure enrich the worshipper! Pure, thou dost strike the Vritras dead, and strivest pure, to win the spoil.
Chapter II · Hymn 9.3
Eager for wealth we meditate Agni's effectual laud to-day, Laud of the God who touches heaven.
Chapter II · Hymn 10.1
May Agni who is Hotar-priest among mankind accept our songs, And worship the celestial folk!
Chapter II · Hymn 10.2
Thou, Agni, art spread widely forth, Priest dear and excellent through thee Men make the sacrifice complete.
Chapter II · Hymn 10.3
To him, praiseworthy, sacred tones have sounded, Steer of the triple height, the life- bestower. Dwelling in wood, like Varuna, a river, lavishing treasure, he distributes blessings.
Chapter II · Hymn 11.1
Great conqueror, warrior girt, Lord of all heroes, flow on thy way as he who winneth riches: With sharpened arms, with swift bow, never vanquished in battle, vanquishing in fight the foemen!
Chapter II · Hymn 11.2
Giving security, Lord of wide dominion, send us both heaven and earth with all their fulness! Striving to win the Dawns, the light, the waters, and cattle, call to us abundant booty!
Chapter II · Hymn 11.3
O Indra, thou art far-renowned, impetuous Lord of power and might. Alone, the never-conquered guardian of mankind, thou smitest down resistless foes.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.1

Thee have we chosen, skilfullest in sacrifice, immortal, Priest, among the Gods, Best finisher of this holy rite:
Chapter II · Hymn 13.1
The Waters' Child, the blessed brightly-shining one, Agni whose, light is excellent. May he by sacrifice win us in heaven the grace of Mitra, Varuna, and the Floods!
Chapter II · Hymn 13.2
Lord of all food is he, the man whom thou protectest in the fight, Agni, and urgest to the fray.
Chapter II · Hymn 14.1
Him, whosoever he may be, no one may vanquish, mighty one! Nay, very glorious wealth is his.
Chapter II · Hymn 14.2
May he who dwells with all mankind conquer in fight with steeds of war, With sages may he win the spoil.

Ten sisters, pouring out the rain together, the sage's quickly moving thoughts, adorn him. Hither hath run the gold-hued Child of Surya, and reached the vat like a fleet vigorous courser.
Chapter II · Hymn 15.1
Even as a youngling shouting with his mothers, the bounteous Steer hath flowed along with waters. As youth to damsel, so with milk he hastens on to the settled meeting-place, the beaker.

Chapter II · Hymn 15.3
Drink, Indra, of the savoury juice, and cheer thee, with our milky draught! Be, for our weal, our friend and sharer of the feast, and let thy wisdom guard us well!
Chapter II · Hymn 16.1
In thy kind grace and favour may we still be strong: cast us not down before the foe! With manifold assistance guard and succour us, and stablish us in thy good-will!

Chapter II · Hymn 17.1

Chapter II · Hymn 17.2

May those his brilliant rays be ever free from death, inviolate for both classes of created things-- Rays wherewith powers of men and Gods are purified! Yea, even for this have sages welcomed him as King.
Chapter II · Hymn 17.3
Lauded with song, to feast him, flow to Vayu, flow purified to Varuna and Mitra! Flow to the song inspiring car-borne hero, to mighty Indra, him who wields the thunder!

Chapter II · Hymn 18.3
When thou, unequalled Maghavan, wast born to smite the Vritras dead, Thou spreadest out the spacious earth and didst support and prop the heavens.
Chapter II · Hymn 19.1
Then was the sacrifice produced for thee, the laud, and song of joy. In might thou art above this All, all that now is and yet shall be.
Chapter II · Hymn 19.2
Raw kine thou filledst with ripe milk. Thou madest Surya rise to heaven. Heat him as milk is heated with pure Sdma hymns, great joy to him who loves the song!
Chapter II · Hymn 19.3
Rejoice: thy glory hath been quaffed, Lord of bay steeds! as 'twere the bowl's enlivening mead. Thine, Steer, is Indu, Steer, the Strong, best winner of a thousand spoils.
Chapter II · Hymn 20.1
Let our strong drink, most excellent, exhilarating, come to thee, Victorious, Indra! bringing gain, immortal conquering in fight!
Chapter II · Hymn 20.2
Thou, hero, winner of the spoil, urgest to speed the car of man. Burn, like a vessel with the flame, the riteless Dasyu, conqueror!

Pour down the rain upon us, pour a wave of waters from the sky. And plenteous store of wholesome foood!

Dearest to Gods in sacred rites, pour on us fatness with thy stream, Pour down on us a flood of rain!
Chapter III · Hymn 1.3
To give as vigour, with thy stream run through the fleecy straining-cloth! For verily the Gods will hear.
Chapter III · Hymn 1.4
Onward hath Pavamana flowed and beaten off the Rakshasas. Flashing out splendour as of old.

Bring forth oblations to the God who knoweth all, who fain would drink. The wanderer, lagging not behind the hero, coming nigh with, speed!

With Somas go ye nigh to him chief drinker of the Soma's. juice: With beakers to the impetuous God, to Indra with the flowing, drops!

Purify Soma when effused with stones which hands move rapidly, And pour the sweet milk in the meath.

O Soma Pavamana, give us riches and heroic strength, Indu, with Indra. our ally!

Surya, thou mountest up to meet the hero famous for his wealth, Who hurls the bolt and works for men;

Him who with might of both his arms broke nine-and-ninety castles down, Slew Vritra and smote Ahi dead.

This Indra is our gracious friend. He sends, like a full-streaming cow, Riches in horses, kine, and corn.

Radiant, as high Truth, cherished, best at winning strength, Truth based upon the statute that supports the heavens, He rose, a light that kills Vritras and enemies, best slayer of the Dasyus, Asuras, and foes.

Protect us, Indra, each to-day, each to morrow, and each following day! Through all the days shalt thou, Lord of the brave, preserve our singers both by day and night!
Chapter III · Hymn 7.1
A crushing warrior, passing rich, is Maghavan, endowed with all heroic strength. Thine arms, O Satakratu, are exceeding strong, those arms, which grasp the thunderbolt.

We call upon Sarasvan as unmarried men who long for wives, As bounteous men who yearn for sons.

Chapter III · Hymn 9.1
May we attain that excellent glory of Savitar the God: So may he stimulate our prayers!
Chapter III · Hymn 10.1
O Brahmanaspati, make thou Kakshivan Ausija a loud Chanter of flowing Soma juice!
Chapter III · Hymn 10.2
Agni, thou pourest life: send down upon us food and vigorous strength; Drive thou misfortune far away!
Chapter III · Hymn 10.3
So help ye us to riches, great celestial and terrestrial wealth Vast is your sway among the Gods!
Chapter III · Hymn 11.1
Carefully tending Law with law they have attained their vigorous might: Both Gods, devoid of guile, wax strong.
Chapter III · Hymn 11.2
With rainy skies and streaming floods, Lords of the food that falls in dew, A lofty seat have they attained.
Chapter III · Hymn 11.3
They who stand round him as he moves harness the bright, the ruddy steed: The lights shining in the sky.

On both sides to the car they yoke the two bay coursers dear to him, Brown, bold, who bear the hero on.

Thou, making light where no light was, and form, O men where form was not, Wast born together with the Dawns.

Chapter III · Hymn 13.2
Flow onward like the potent band of Maruts, like that celestial host which none revileth! Quickly be gracious unto us like waters, like sacrifice victorious, thousand-fashioned!
Chapter III · Hymn 13.3
O Agni, thou hast been ordained Hotar of every sacrifice, By Gods, among the race of men. So with sweet-sounding tongues for us sacrifice nobly in this rite: Bring thou the Gods and worship them
Chapter III · Hymn 14.1
For, as disposer, Agni, God, most wise in sacrifices, thou Knowest straightway the roads and paths.
Chapter III · Hymn 14.3
Immortal, Hotar-priest, and God, with wondrous power heleads the way, Urging the congregations on.
Chapter III · Hymn 15.1
Strong, he is set on deeds of strength. He is led forth in holy rites, Sage who completes the sacrifice.
Chapter III · Hymn 15.2
Excellent, he was made by thought. The germ of beings have gained. Yea, and the Sire of active power.
Chapter III · Hymn 15.3
Pour on the juice the heated milk which hasteneth to heaven and. earth; Bestow the liquid on the Bull!

These know their own abiding-place: like calves beside themother cows, They come together with their kin.
Chapter III · Hymn 16.2
Devouring in their greedy jaws, they make sustaining food irb heaven, For Indra, Agni, homage, light.

In all the worlds That was the best and highest whence sprang the mighty one, of splendid valour, As soon as he is born he smites his foemen, he in whom all who lend him aid are joyful foe
Chapter III · Hymn 17.1
Grown mighty in his strength, of ample vigour, he as a strikes fear into the Dasa, Eager to win the breathing and the breathless. All sang thy praise at banquet and oblation.
Chapter III · Hymn 17.2

Chapter III · Hymn 17.3

Chapter III · Hymn 18.1

Give us a share of wealth most high, a share of wealth most near to us, A share of wealth that is between.

I from my Father have obtained deep knowledge of eternal Law; I was born like unto the Sun.

After the ancient manner I, like Kanva, beautify my songs, And Indra's self gains power thereby.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.2
Whatever gishis have not praised thee, Indra, or have praised thee, wax Mighty indeed when praised by me!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.3
Agni, produced by strength, do thou with all thy fires accept our prayer: With those that are with Gods, with those that are with men exalt our songs!

Forth come to us with all his fires that Agni, whose the mighty are, Come, fully girt about with wealth for us and for our kith and kin!

Do thou, O Agni, with thy fires strengthen our prayer and sacrifices: Incite them to bestow their wealth to aid our service of the Gods!

Some, the men of old whose grass was trimmed addressed the hymn to thee for mighty strength and for renown: So, hero, urge us onward to heroic power'

Thou didst produce him, deathless one! for mortal man, for maintenance of Law and lovely Amrita: Thou evermore hast moved making wealth flow to us.

Pour out the drops f or Indra; let him drink the meath of Soma Juice! He through his majesty sends forth his bounteous gifts.

Chapter I · Hymn 8.3
Thou wishest for thy kine a bull, lord of thy cows whom none may kill, For those who long for his approach, for those who turn away from him.

The Gods made him the Hotar-priest of sacrifice, oblationbearer, passing wise. Agni gives wealth and valour to the worshipper, to man who offers up his gifts.

He hath appeared, best prosperer, in whom men lay their holy acts: So may our songs of praise come nigh to Agni who was born to give the Arya strength.

Him before whom the people shrink when he performs his glorious deeds, Him who wins thousands at the sacrifice, himself, that Agni, reverence with songs!

Agni of Divoddsa, God, comes forth like Indra in his might. Rapidly hath he moved along his mother earth; he stands in high heaven's dwelling-place.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.3
Agni, thou pourest life: send down upon us food and vigorous strength: Drive thou misfortune far away!

Skilled in thy task, O Agni, pour splendour with hero strength on us, Granting me wealth that nourishes!
Chapter I · Hymn 12.3
O Agni, holy and divine with splendour and thy pleasant tongue. Bring thou the Gods and worship them!

Agni is wakened: Surya riseth from the earth. Bright Dawn hath opened out the mighty twain with light. The Asvins have equipped their chariot for the course. God Savitar hath roused the world in sundry ways.
Chapter III · Hymn 17.1
When, O ye Asvins, ye equip your mighty car, with fatness and with honey balm, ye twain, our power! To our devotion give victorious strength in war: may we win riches in the heroes' strife for spoil!
Chapter III · Hymn 17.2

Nigh to us come the Asvins' lauded three wheeled car, the car laden with meath and drawn by fleet-foot steeds, Three-seated, opulent, bestowing all delight: may it bring weal to us, to cattle and to men!
Chapter III · Hymn 17.3
Thy streams that never fail or waste flow forth like showers of rain from heaven, To bring a thousand stores of wealth.
Chapter III · Hymn 18.1
He, flows beholding on his way all well-beloved sacred lore, Green-tinted, brandishing his arms.
Chapter III · Hymn 18.2
He, when the people deck him like a docile king of elephants, Sits as a falcon in the wood.
Chapter III · Hymn 18.3
So bring thou hitherward to us, Indu, while thou art purified. All treasures both of heaven and earth!
Chapter III · Hymn 18.4
9: Forward have flowed the streams of power, of this the mighty one effused, Of him who waits upon the Gods.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.1
The singers praise him with their song, and learned priests adorn the steed Born as thelight that merits laud.
Chapter I · Hymn 1.2
These things thou winnest quickly, while men cleanse thee, Soma, nobly rich!
Chapter I · Hymn 1.3
This Brahman, comer at the due time, named Indra, is renowned and praised.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.1
To thee alone, O Lord of Strength, go, as it were, all songs of praise.
Chapter I · Hymn 2.2
Like streams of water on their way, let bounties, Indra, flow from thee!
Chapter I · Hymn 2.3
Even as a car to give us aid, we draw thee nigh to favour us, Strong in thy deeds, quelling attack, Indra, Lord, mightiest! of the brave.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.1
Great in thou power and wisdom, strong, with thought that comprehendeth all! Wide hast thou spread in majesty.
Chapter I · Hymn 3.2
Thou very mighty one, whose hands by virtue of thy greatness wield The golden bolt that beaks its way!
Chapter I · Hymn 3.3
He who hath lighted up the joyous castle, wise courser like the steed of cloudy heaven, Bright like the Sun with hundredfold existence
Chapter I · Hymn 4.1
He, doubly born, hath spread in his effulgence through the three luminous realms, through all the regions, Best sacrificing Priest where waters gather.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.2
Priest doubly born, he through his love of glory hath in his keeping all things worth the choosing. The man who brings him gifts hath noble offspring.
Chapter I · Hymn 4.3
Agni, with hymns may we now accomplish that which thou lovest, Strength, like a horse auspicious, with service!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.1
For, Agni, thou art now the promoter of strength auspicious, Lofty sacrifice, power effective.
Chapter I · Hymn 5.2
Through these our praises, come thou to meet us, bright as the sunlight, Agni, kindly with all thy faces!
Chapter I · Hymn 5.3
Immortal Jatavedas, thou bright-hued refulgent gift of Dawn. Agni, this day to him who pays oblations bring the Gods who waken with the morn!
Chapter I · Hymn 6.1
For thou art offering-bearer, well-loved messenger, and charioteer of holy rites. Accordant with the Asvins and with Dawn grant us heroic strength and lofty fame!
Chapter I · Hymn 6.2
The old hath waked the young Moon from his slumber who runs his circling course with many round him Behold the God's high wisdom in its greatness: he who died yesterday to-day is living.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.1
Strong is the red Bird in his strength, great hero, who from of old bath had no nest to dwell in. That which he knows is truth and never idle: he wins and gives the wealth desired of many.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.2

Through these Thunderer gained strong manly vigour, through whom he waxed in stren gth to slaughter Vritra; These who through might of actual operation sprang forth as Gods in course of Law and Order.
Chapter I · Hymn 7.3
Here is the Soma ready pressed: of this the Maruts, yea, of this Self-luminous, the Asvins, drink.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.1
Of this, moreover, purified, set in three places, procreant, Drink Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman.
Chapter I · Hymn 8.2
Yea, Indra, like the Hotar-priest, will in the early morning drink, At pleasure, of the milky juice:
Chapter I · Hymn 8.3
Verily, Surya, thou art great; truly, Aditya, thou art great. O most admired for greatness of thy majesty, God, by thy greatn.ess thou art great.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.1
Yea, Surya, thou art great in fame: thou evermore, O God, art great. Thou by thy greatness art the Gods' High-Priest, divine, farspread unconquerable light.
Chapter I · Hymn 9.2
Come, Lord of rapturous joys, to our libations with thy bay steeds, come With bay steeds to our flowing juice!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.1
Known as best Vritra-slayer erst, as Indra $atakratu, come With bay steeds to our flowing juice!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.2
For, Vritra-slayer, thou art he who drinks these drops of Soma come With bay steeds to our flowing juice!
Chapter I · Hymn 10.3
Bring to the wise, the great, who waxeth mighty your offerings and make ready your devotion. Go forth to many tribes as man's controller!
Chapter I · Hymn 11.1
For Indra the sublime, the far-pervading, have singers generateo prayer and praises; The sages never violate his statutes.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.2
The choirs have established Indra King for ever for victory him, whose anger is resistless: And for the bays' Lord strengthened those he loveth.
Chapter I · Hymn 11.3
If I, O Indra, were the lord of riches ample as thine own, I would support the singer, God who scatterest wealth! and, not abandon him to woe.
Chapter I · Hymn 12.1
Each day would I enrich the man who sang my praise, in whatsoever place he were. No kinship is there better, Maghavan, than thine: a father even, is no more.
Chapter I · Hymn 12.2
Here thou the call of the juice-drinking press-stone: mark thou the sage's hymn who sings and lauds thee! Take to thine inmost self these adorations!
Chapter I · Hymn 13.1
I know and ne'er forget the hymns and praises of thee, theconqueror, of thy power immortal. Thy name I ever utter, self-refulgent!
Chapter I · Hymn 13.2
Among mankind many are thy libations, and many a time the pious sage invokes thee. O Maghavan, be not long distant from us!
Chapter I · Hymn 13.3

Sing strength to Indra that shall. set his chariot in the foremost place! Giver of room in closest fight, slayer of foes in shock of war, be thou our great encorager! Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of our weak mies!
Chapter I · Hymn 14.1

Thou didst destroy the Dragon: thou sentest the rivers down to Earth. Foeless, O Indra, wast thou born. Thou tendest well each choicest thing. Therefore we draw us close to thee. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of our weak enemies! Destroyed be all malignitics and all our enemy's designs!
Chapter I · Hymn 14.2
Thy bolt thou castest at the foe, O Indra, who would smite us dead: thy liberal bounty gives us wealth. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of our weak enemies!
Chapter I · Hymn 14.3
Rich be the praiser of one rich and liberal, Lord of days! like thee: High rank be his who lauds the juice!
Chapter I · Hymn 15.1
His wealth who hath no store of kine hath ne'er found out recited laud, Nor song of praises that is sung.
Chapter I · Hymn 15.2
Give us not, Indra, as a prey unto the scornful or the proud: Help, mighty one, with power and might!
Chapter I · Hymn 15.3
Come hither, Indra, with thy bays, come thou to Kanva's eulogy! Ye by command of yonder Dyaus, God bright by day! have gone to heaven.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.1
The stones' rim shakes the Soma here like a wolf worrying a sheep. Ye by command of yonder Dyaus, God bright by day I have gone to heaven.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.2
May the stone bring thee as it speaks, the Soma-stone with ringing voice! Ye by command of yonder Dyaus, God bright by day! have gone to heaven.
Chapter I · Hymn 16.3
For Indra flow most rich in sweets, O Soma, bringing him delight!
Chapter I · Hymn 17.1
Bright, meditating sacred song, these juices have sent Vayu forth.
Chapter I · Hymn 17.2
They were sent forth to feast the Gods, like chariots speeding in the race.
Chapter I · Hymn 17.3

Agni I deem our Hotar priest, munificent wealth-giver, Son of Strength, who knoweth all that is even as the Sage who knoweth all. Lord of fair rites, a God with form erected turning to the Gods, he when the flame hath sprung forth from the holy oil, the offered fatness, longs for it as it grows bright.
Chapter I · Hymn 18.1

We, sacrificing, call on the best worshipper thee eldest of Angirasas, singer! with hyrnns, thee, brilliant one! with singers' hymn; Thee, wandering round, as 'twere the sky, thee who art Hotar-priest of men, whom, Bull with hair of flame, the people must observe, tile people that he speed them on.
Chapter I · Hymn 18.2

He with his blazing Power refulgent far and wide, he verily it iswho conquers demon foes, conquers the demons like an axe: At whose close touch things solid partg and what is stable yields he keeps his ground and flinches not,like trees. Subduing all from the skilled archer flinches not.
Chapter I · Hymn 18.3
O Agni, strength and fame are thine: thy fires blaze forth on high, O thou refulgent God! Sage, passing bright, thou givest to the worshipper with power, the wealth that merits laud.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.1
With brilliantg purifying sheen, with perfect sheen thou liftest up thyself in light. Thou, visiting both thy mothers, aidest them as son; thou joinest close the earth and heaven.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.2
O Jatavedas, Son of Strength, rejoice thyself, gracious, in our fair hymns and songs! In thee have they heaped viands various, many formed; wealthborn, of wondrous help are they.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.3
Agni, spread forth, as ruler, over living things: give wealth, to us, immortal God! Thou shinest out from beauty fair to look upon: thou leadest us to beauteous Power.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.4
I laud the Sage, who orders sacrifice, who hath great riches under his control. Thou givest blest award of good, and plenteous food, thou givest wealth that wins success.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.5
The men have set before them, for his favour, Agni, strong, visible to all, the holy. Thee, Lord divine, with ears to hear, most famous, mens' generations magnify with praise-songs.
Chapter II · Hymn 1.6
Agni, he conquers by thine aid that brings him store of valiant sons and does great deeds, Whose bond of friendship is thy choice.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.1
Thy spark is black and crackling; kindled in due time, O bounteous, it is taken up. Thou art the dear friend of the mighty Mornings: thou shinest in glimmerings of the night.
Chapter II · Hymn 2.2
Him, duly coming, as their germ have plants received: this Agni have maternal Waters brought to life. So, in like manner, do the forest trees and plants bear him within them and produce him evermore.
Chapter II · Hymn 3.1
Agni grows bright for Indra: he shines far resplendent in the sky: He sends forth offspring like a queen.
Chapter II · Hymn 4.1
The sacred hymns love him who wakes and watches: to him who watches the holy verses. This Soma saith to him Who wake my dwelling in thy friendship.
Chapter II · Hymn 5.1
Agni is watchful, and the Richas love him: Agni is watchful, Sama hymns approach him. Agni is watchful, to him saith this Soma, I rest and have my dwelling in thy friendship.
Chapter II · Hymn 6.1
Praise to the friends who sit in front! to those seated together,praise I use the hundred-footed speech speech.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.1
I use the hundred-footed speech, I sing what hath a thousand paths, Gayatra, Trishtup, Jagat hymn.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.2
Gayatra, Trishtup, Jagat hymn,the forms united and complete, Have the Gods made familiar friends.
Chapter II · Hymn 7.3
Agni, is light, light is Agni, Indra is light, light is Indra Surya is light, light is Surya.
Chapter II · Hymn 8.1
O Agni, turn again with strength, turn thou again with food and life: Save us again from grief and woe!
Chapter II · Hymn 8.2
O Agni, turn again with wealth sprinkle thou us from everyside. With thine own all-supporting stream!
Chapter II · Hymn 8.3
If I, O Indra, were like thee, the single ruler over wealth. My worshipper should be rich in kine.
Chapter II · Hymn 9.1
I should be fain, O Lord of power, to strengthen and enrich thesage, Where I the ford of herds of kine.
Chapter II · Hymn 9.2
Thy goodness, Indra, is a cow yielding in plenty kine and steeds. To worshippers who press the juice.
Chapter II · Hymn 9.3
Yea, Waters, ye bring health and bliss: so help ye us to energy. That we may look on great delight!
Chapter II · Hymn 10.1
Give us a portion of the dew, the most auspicious that ye have, Like mothers in their longing love!
Chapter II · Hymn 10.2
For you we gladly go to hirn to whose abode ye speed us on, And, Waters, give us procreant strength!
Chapter II · Hymn 10.3
May Vata breathe his balm on us, healthful, delightful to our heart: May he prolong our days of life!
Chapter II · Hymn 11.1
Thou art our father, Vata, yea, thou art our brother and our friend: So give us strength that we may live!
Chapter II · Hymn 11.2
The store of Amrit that laid away yonder, O Vata, in thine home-- Give us strength that we may live!
Chapter II · Hymn 11.3
The fleet steed wearing divers forms, the eagle bearing his golden raiment to his birthplace, Clothed in due season with the light of Surya, red, hath begot the sacrifice in person.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.1
Multiform seed he laid in waters, lustre which gathered on the earth and there developed. In the mid-air establishing his greatness, he cries aloud, seed of the vigorous courser.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.2
He hath, enduing thousand robes that suit him, as sacrifice upheld the light of Surya, Giver of ample gifts in hundreds, thousands, supporter of the heavens, earth's Lord and ruler.
Chapter II · Hymn 12.3
They gaze on thee with longing in their spirit, as on a strong-winged bird that mounteth sky-ward; On thee with wings of gold, Varuna's envoy, the Bird that hasteneth to the home of Yama.
Chapter II · Hymn 13.1
Erect, to heaven hath the Gandharva mounted, pointing at us his many-coloured weapons: Clad in sweet raiment beautiful to look on, for he, as light, produceth forms that please us..
Chapter II · Hymn 13.2
When as a spark he cometh ilear the ocean, looking with vulture's eye as Law commandeth, His lustre, joying in its own bright splendour, maketh dear glories in the loftiest region.
Chapter II · Hymn 13.3
Swift, rapidly striking, like a bull who sharpens his horns, terrific, stirring up the people. With eyes that close not, bellowing, sole hero, Indra subdued at once a hundred armies.
Chapter III · Hymn 1.1
With him loud-roaring, ever watchful victcr, bold, hard to overthrow, rouser of battle, Indra. the strong, whose hand bears arrows, conquer, ye heroes, now, now vanquish in the combat!
Chapter III · Hymn 1.2
He rules with those who carry shafts and quivers, Indra who with his band brings hosts together, Foe-conquering strong of arm the Soma-drinker, with mighty bow, shooting with well- laid arrows.
Chapter III · Hymn 1.3
Brihaspati, fly with thy chariot hither, slayer of demons, driving off our foemen! Be thou protector of our cars, destroyer, victor in battle, breaker-up of armies!
Chapter III · Hymn 2.1
Conspicuous. by thy strength, firm, foremost fighter, mighty and fierce, victorious, all-subduing, The Son of Conquest, passing men and heroes, kinewinner, mount thy conquering car, O Indra!
Chapter III · Hymn 2.2
Cleaver of stalls, kine-winner, armed with thunder, who quells an army and with might destroys it-- Follow him, brothers! quit yourselves like heroes, and like this Indra show your zeal and courage!
Chapter III · Hymn 2.3
Piercing with conquering strength the cow-stalls, Indra, pitiless hero with unbounded anger, Victor in fight, unshaken and resistless--may he protect our armies in our battles!
Chapter III · Hymn 3.1
Indra guide these! Brihaspati, and Soma, the guerdon and the sacrifice precede them; And let the banded Maruts march in forefront of heavenly hosts that conquer and demolish!
Chapter III · Hymn 3.2
Ours be the potent host of mighty Indra, King Varuna the Maruts, and Adityas! Uplifted is the shout of Gods who conquer, hightninded Gods who cause the worlds to tremble.
Chapter III · Hymn 3.3
Bristle thou up, O Maghavan, our weapons: excite the spirits, of my warring heroes! Urge on the strong steed's might, O Vyitra-slayer, and let the din of conquering cars go upward
Chapter III · Hymn 4.1
May Indra aid us when our flags are gathered: victorious be ther arrows of our army! May our brave men of war prevail in battle. Ye Gods, protect us in the shout of onset!
Chapter III · Hymn 4.2
That army of the foemen, O ye Maruts, which, striving in its. mighty strength, approaches, Hide ye and bury it in pathless darkness that not a man oF them may know the other!
Chapter III · Hymn 4.3
Bewildering the senses of our foemen, seize thou their bodies, and depart, O Agha! Attack them, set their hearts on fare with sorrows; so let our foes abide in utter darkness!
Chapter III · Hymn 5.1
Advance, O heroes, win the day, May Indra be your sure defence! Mighty and awful be your arms, that none may wound or injure you!
Chapter III · Hymn 5.2
Loosed from the bowstring fly away, thou arrows sharpened by our prayer! Go to the foemen, strike them home, and let not one be left alive!
Chapter III · Hymn 5.3
Let ravens and strong-pinioned birds pursue them: yea, let that army be the food of vultures! Indra, let none escape, no sin-remover: behind them all let following birds be gathered!
Chapter III · Hymn 6.1
This host of foemen Maghavan! that cometh on in warlike show-- Meet it, O Vritra-slayer, thou, Indra, and Agni, with your flames!
Chapter III · Hymn 6.2
There where the flights of arrows fall like boys whose locks are yet unshorn. Even there may Brahmanaspati, may Aditi protect us well, protect us well through all our days!
Chapter III · Hymn 6.3
Drive Rakshasas and foes away, break thou in pieces Vritra's jaws: O Vritra-slaying Indra, quell the foeman's wrath who threatens us!
Chapter III · Hymn 7.1
O Indra, beat our foes away, humble the men who challenge us: Send down to nether darkness him who seeks to do us injury!
Chapter III · Hymn 7.2
Strong, ever-youthful are the arms of Indra, fair unassailable, never to be vanquished: These first let him employ when need hath come on us, wherewith the Asuras' great might was overthrown.
Chapter III · Hymn 7.3
Thy vital parts I cover with thine armour: with immortality King Soma clothe thee! Varuna give thee what is more than ample, and in thy victory may Gods be joyful!
Chapter III · Hymn 8.1
Blind, O my foemen, shall ye be, even as headless serpents are May Indra slay each best of you when Agni's flame hath struck you down!
Chapter III · Hymn 8.2
Whoso would kill us, whether he be a stranger foe or one of us, May all the Gods discomfit him! My nearest, closest mail is prayer, my closest armour and defence.
Chapter III · Hymn 8.3
Like a dread wild beast roaming on the mountain thou hast approached us from the farthest distance. Whetting thy bolt and thy sharp blade, O Indra, crush thou the foe and scatter those who hate us!
Chapter III · Hymn 9.1
Gods, may our ears hear that which is auspicious, may our eyes see that which is good, ye holy! Extolling you with still strong limbs and bodies, may we attain the age by Gods appointed!
Chapter III · Hymn 9.2

Illustrious far and wide, may Indra bless us, may Pushan bless us, master of all riches! May Tarkshya with uninjured fellies bless us! Brihaspati bestow on us his favour! Brihaspati bestow on us his favour!
